p: Most day trips work reef country within about 15 nautical miles of the coast, so there's plenty of fishing time without a huge run. On calmer days and longer trips, boats head for the southern reefs of the Capricorn and Bunker Group, which lies roughly 45–75 km from the coastal departure ports.

p: You can fish 1770 all year, but local anglers rate the cooler months highest for the reef: bites improve as the water cools and the currents ease, and sharks are less of a problem around the outer reefs.

Best from about May to October, when schools gather on the pinnacles off Fitzroy Reef

sections.h: Departure points and the Round Hill Creek bar
p: Charters leave from the Town of 1770 on Captain Cook Drive — from the marina, the public boat ramp and pontoon on Round Hill Creek, or by tender from the beach at the 1770 camping grounds. The creek mouth is very shallow and the bar moves constantly, so departure and return times are set around the tide. Operators check the tide height before confirming a trip, and VMR Round Hill can advise on current bar conditions.

Most of the offshore grounds are inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones, especially on the western side. Charter skippers fish the open zones; if you're on your own boat, check the official GBRMPA zoning map rather than relying on the map at the ramp. Eurimbula Creek is a mud crab sanctuary.

Getting there: Agnes Water is about 5.5 hours' drive from Brisbane, around 1 hour 25 minutes from Bundaberg and 1 hour 30 minutes from Gladstone. The nearest airports are Bundaberg and Gladstone, and Greyhound coaches stop in Agnes Water daily. If you'd like more choice of boats, Bundaberg and Gladstone charters also fish the southern reefs.

Hooked On 1770 is the town's listed day charter, running half- and full-day reef trips plus private and custom charters on Hooked on 2. Its published rates are $320 per person for a half day and $450 for a full day, with private charters for up to seven quoted on request. The business is restructuring, so trip dates are released at short notice; register your dates on its calendar. If nothing is running, Bundaberg and Gladstone boats also fish the southern reefs.

faq: How far out is the reef from 1770?

Some of the reef fishing is close: charters work deep-water reefs within about 15 nautical miles of 1770. The Capricorn and Bunker Group, including Lady Musgrave Island and Fitzroy Reef, lies roughly 45–75 km from the coastal ports, so those trips are longer days.
Why do fishing charter times at 1770 depend on the tide?

Boats leave through Round Hill Creek, where the bar is shallow and keeps shifting. Operators time departures and returns for enough water over the bar and may reschedule if the tide is too low at the planned time.
Can you fish around Lady Musgrave Island?

In parts. Much of the Capricorn and Bunker Group is green zone, where fishing isn't allowed, but there are open zones around the reefs. Charter skippers know where you can fish; private boaties should check the GBRMPA zoning map first.
Is 1770 a good place to catch red emperor?
Yes — the area is known for it. Schools of red emperor gather on deep pinnacles east of Fitzroy Reef, mainly from about May to October, and they're also caught on the closer deep-water reefs.
Do I need to bring my own fishing gear?
No. Day charters from 1770 supply rods, reels, bait and tackle. Bring food and drinks if they're not included, sun protection and an esky for your catch.
agnes-water.season: 1770 fishes year-round, but locals rate the cooler months (about May to October) best for reef fish, with red emperor schooling on the Fitzroy Reef pinnacles. Cobia, tuna and trevally are on the wrecks all year. Note the closures: coral reef fin fish 8–12 October and 6–10 November (2026), snapper and pearl perch 15 July–15 August, and barramundi 1 November–31 January.
intro: The Town of 1770 and neighbouring Agnes Water sit where the Great Barrier Reef begins, about halfway between Bundaberg and Gladstone. Charter boats leave Round Hill Creek for deep-water reefs within about 15 nautical miles of the coast, the rocks off Bustard Head, trawler wrecks, and on longer days the southern reefs of the Capricorn and Bunker Group such as Lady Musgrave Island and Fitzroy Reef.

Reef trips target coral trout, red emperor, red throat emperor, nannygai and sweetlip, with cobia, mackerel and tuna around the wrecks. Closer in, Round Hill, Eurimbula, Middle and Pancake creeks hold mangrove jack, barramundi, queenfish, grunter and whiting. Departures are timed around the tide because the Round Hill Creek bar is shallow and always shifting.

mary-river.summary: Mary River fishing charters either collect you from Darwin at about 5am or launch at the Shady Camp ramp near Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge. Barramundi are the target, with saratoga in the billabongs and threadfin salmon below the barrage. The late February–May run-off brings the biggest barra. Guided trips cost about $230–$750 per person; private boats about $2,200–$2,300.
intro: The Mary River wetlands east of Darwin are some of the Territory's most famous barramundi water. Charters fish from the Shady Camp ramp — where a barrage separates the fresh and salt water — down towards the river mouth, as well as billabongs like Corroboree, part of the Mary system and about 90 minutes from Darwin.

As well as barramundi, anglers catch threadfin salmon, jewfish and, in the billabongs, saratoga. NT tourism notes that barra up to 1.4m are landed in the wetlands each year. The system also holds one of Australia's largest concentrations of saltwater crocodiles, which is one reason most visitors fish it with an experienced local guide.
mary-river.season: The run-off from late February to May — peaking in March and April — is the time for big barramundi below the Shady Camp barrage and at the creek mouths. The build-up (September to mid-December) is the other big-fish window, while the dry season gives consistent billabong fishing for barra, saratoga and tarpon.

sections.h: Where the Mary River charters fish
p: The Mary River system lets one trip fish both fresh and salt water. Above the Shady Camp barrage are permanent, lily-lined billabongs; below it the tidal river splits into Sampan and Tommycut creeks and runs into Chambers Bay.

p: The Mary is fished most of the year, but the seasons change where and how you fish.

p: The Mary River is east of Darwin via the Stuart and Arnhem Highways. Corroboree Billabong is about 108 km from Darwin, and Shady Camp is about 200 km — around 1 hour 40 minutes by car, or about two hours towing a boat. Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge, 20 minutes from Shady Camp, is reachable on sealed road almost all the way.

Most visitors fish with a Darwin-based guide on a day trip — pick-up from your Darwin accommodation is usually about 5am, fishing Corroboree or Shady Camp and returning mid to late afternoon. In the run-off, many guides run multi-day trips based at a lodge near Shady Camp.
items: Corroboree Billabong day trip
About 108 km from Darwin; full days with 4:30–5am pick-up, about $400–$575 per person shared
Shady Camp day trip
About 200 km from Darwin; longer days (about 10–11 hours door to door) from Darwin, or half and full days from Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge
Run-off packages (March–May)
2–7 day trips based at Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge or on a mothership at Shady Camp, with meals, transfers and gear
Self-drive
Point Stuart hires a 4.1 m dinghy for four at the Shady Camp ramp; houseboats and fishing dinghies can also be hired in the area

p: The Mary River has its own fish management zone. NT Fisheries sets a limit of three barramundi per person (minimum 55 cm), with only one fish over 90 cm per vessel, and bans cast nets and drag nets. Within 100 m of the Shady Camp barrage wall you may fish only with a lure or fly on a single-point hook. Recreational fishing below the barrage is open year-round. Check the current NT Fisheries rules before you go; your guide will also brief you.

You'll need an NT Parks Visitor Pass to enter Mary River National Park (NT residents are exempt), and campsites at Shady Camp must be booked online. NT tourism says the river holds up to 15 saltwater crocodiles per kilometre, one of the highest densities in the world: don't swim, stay well back from the water's edge, and never wade in to free a snagged lure.

faq: How far is the Mary River from Darwin?

Corroboree Billabong is about 108 km east of Darwin, and Shady Camp is about 200 km, roughly 1 hour 40 minutes by car (about two hours towing a boat) via the Stuart and Arnhem Highways. Most guided day trips pick up from Darwin accommodation at around 4:30–5am.
Can I do a Mary River fishing trip as a day trip from Darwin?

Yes. Several Darwin guides, including Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters, DNA Barra Fishing, Obsession, Offshore Boats and River & Reef, run full days to Corroboree Billabong or Shady Camp with accommodation pick-up, returning mid to late afternoon. Shared seats cost about $400–$575 per person. Run-off trips are often multi-day and based at a lodge near Shady Camp.
Should I fish Shady Camp or Corroboree Billabong?

Corroboree is closer to Darwin and a lily-lined freshwater billabong system with about 45 km of water, best in the dry season for barra, saratoga and tarpon. Shady Camp is further but lets one trip fish both the freshwater billabong and the tidal river, and it is where the biggest run-off barra are caught below the barrage and at the creek mouths.
Is there a closed season or special barra limit on the Mary River?

There is no closed season below the Shady Camp barrage; it has been open year-round since 2014. The Mary River fish management zone does have its own rules: three barramundi per person (minimum 55 cm), one over 90 cm per vessel, and no cast or drag nets. Check the current NT Fisheries rules before keeping fish.
Can you fish from the bank at Shady Camp?

Yes. The barrage is a well-known land-based spot, but within 100 m of the barrage wall only a lure or fly on a single-point hook is allowed, so no bait or treble hooks. Crocodile numbers are very high, so keep well back from the edge.
Do I need a park pass for the Mary River?
Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass for Mary River National Park; NT residents are exempt. Campsites, including at Shady Camp, must be booked online before you arrive.
Are Mary River fishing trips good for beginners and kids?

Yes, with the right trip. Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge offers casting, trolling and fly tuition for first-timers from the Shady Camp ramp, and Estuary Escapes coaches novice anglers. Barra Private Tours takes children from age 5 on day trips and age 8 on its multi-day Shady Camp packages. Darwin day trips start with a pick-up at about 4:30–5am, so plan for an early night.
Can I book a shared seat or do I need a private boat?

Both are available. Shared seats suit solo anglers and couples: Point Stuart's guided half day is $230 per person and Darwin day tours are about $400–$750 per person. A private boat for up to four costs about $2,200–$2,300 a day with Barra Private Tours or Alure. Some trips need a minimum of two guests.

intro: Central Coast charters launch from The Haven at Terrigal and are on the offshore reefs within minutes, fishing for snapper, jewfish, kingfish, teraglin, morwong, flathead and John Dory. Game boats run to Browns Mountain, the Norah Head Canyons and the continental shelf, about 23 nautical miles out.

Further south, Hardys Bay on Broken Bay gives access to the reefs and wrecks off the Bouddi Peninsula, with sheltered water inside the bay when it's windy outside. Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney, which makes the Central Coast an easy day trip from the city.
central-coast.season: Reef fishing from Terrigal runs all year for snapper, jewfish, kingfish and morwong. Summer adds mahi mahi and the game season for marlin, yellowfin tuna and albacore, with local crews preferring to tag and release marlin. Terrigal Fishing Tours runs its fishing charters only from December to April, so check seasons before you plan.

p: Central Coast charters work two different stretches of water. From The Haven at Terrigal, boats are on the offshore reefs within minutes, and game boats can run to the continental shelf, about 23 nautical miles out. From Hardys Bay on Broken Bay, charters fish the reefs and wrecks off the Bouddi Peninsula, or stay inside the bay around the headlands when the wind is up.

Norah Head Canyons

Bouddi Peninsula reefs and wrecks
Reached from Hardys Bay; snapper, flathead, bream, jewfish, kingfish and tailor
Broken Bay headlands
Calm-water option for families and windy days

p: Reef fishing from Terrigal runs all year. Summer adds mahi mahi and the game season for marlin, yellowfin tuna and albacore; local game crews prefer to tag and release marlin. One Hardys Bay operator runs fishing charters only in the summer months, December to April, so check seasons before you plan a trip.

p: Licensed charter boats carry a block licence or fee-exemption certificate, so guests don't need their own NSW recreational fishing licence aboard. Shared trips need minimum numbers (five on one Central Coast boat), so wait until the trip is confirmed before booking accommodation.
Seasickness isn't grounds for a refund, and boats won't return early for one passenger, so take medication before you board. Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney.

faq: Can you still fish from the Central Coast when it's too rough offshore?
Often, yes. Hardys Bay charters can stay inside Broken Bay to fish the headlands and estuaries in calmer water, which is why one operator says its kids' trips are rarely cancelled for weather.
Where are the game-fishing grounds off the Central Coast?

Terrigal game boats fish Browns Mountain to the south and the Norah Head Canyons to the north. The continental shelf is about 23 nautical miles offshore, within range of boats qualified to 30 nautical miles.
Do Central Coast fishing charters run all year?
Reef charters from Terrigal run year-round, but at least one Hardys Bay operator runs fishing charters only from December to April, so check the season when booking.
How do I get to Terrigal for a fishing charter?

Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney. Take the Gosford exit off the M1 Pacific Motorway, follow the signs to Terrigal, and turn into The Haven at the south end of the beach, past the football field to the boat ramp.

intro: Newcastle's charters are small-boat estuary guides. They fish the Hunter River from Newcastle Harbour upstream towards Raymond Terrace, and Lake Macquarie, which NSW DPI describes as Australia's largest coastal saltwater lake, joined to the sea by the narrow Swansea Channel.

Guides chase dusky flathead and mulloway on lures and bait, and kingfish around Swansea Bridge and the 'Drop Over' where the channel meets the lake. Lake Macquarie hasn't been commercially netted since 2002, and protected water means seasickness isn't a worry, so it suits families and first-timers. Trips are private, for up to three or four anglers.
newcastle.season: The estuary fishery runs all year. Dusky flathead and mulloway are the signature targets, with flathead best in the warmer months and twilight trips aimed at mulloway. Kingfish hang around Swansea Bridge and the channel, and schools of Australian salmon settle in Swansea Channel in the cooler months.

p: Newcastle's charters are mostly small-boat estuary guides. They fish the Hunter River from Newcastle Harbour upstream towards Raymond Terrace, and Lake Macquarie, a coastal lake of more than 100 sq km joined to the sea by the narrow Swansea Channel.

p: Lake Macquarie hasn't been commercially fished or netted since 2002, and NSW bag and size limits apply. Some Newcastle guides fish lures only and promote catch and release, so ask before booking if you want to keep a feed.
Newcastle is at least two hours' drive north of central Sydney on the M1, and Newcastle Airport at Williamtown has flights from major Australian cities.

faq: Is there a calm-water fishing charter in Newcastle for kids?

Yes. Capn's Charters runs a three-hour kids' charter in calm water on the Hunter River for three children aged 6–16, or two kids and an adult, and Day Trippin fishes sheltered Lake Macquarie with up to four guests.
Where are kingfish caught near Swansea?
Around Swansea Bridge and the 'Drop Over', where the channel meets Lake Macquarie, on surface lures or live bait.
Can you go offshore fishing from Newcastle?

The Newcastle charters listed here fish the Hunter River and Lake Macquarie rather than offshore. NSW DPI's Newcastle Offshore Artificial Reef, in about 28.5 m, is expected to hold kingfish, snapper, silver trevally and mulloway. For a guided reef or game day, the nearest listed charters are at Port Stephens and Terrigal.
How big is Lake Macquarie?
NSW DPI describes it as Australia's largest coastal saltwater lake. It covers more than 100 sq km, is about 24 km long, and has 29 public boat ramps around a 174 km foreshore.

intro: Port Stephens, about 2.5 hours' drive north of Sydney, is one of the few places where blue, black and striped marlin can all be caught in a day, and it hosts the NSW Interclub, Australia's biggest game fishing tournament. Boats run out through Tomaree and Yacaaba heads to Cabbage Tree, Little and Broughton islands, the FADs about 20 km out and the continental shelf.

Inside the heads, the port is a large, sheltered marine-park estuary fed by the Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry systems, where guides chase flathead, bream, whiting, mulloway and even longtail tuna. Most charters leave d'Albora Marinas at Nelson Bay, with others based at Corlette and Soldiers Point.
port-stephens.season: Summer is marlin time: striped and black marlin and mahi mahi work the FADs from about December to March, blue marlin patrol the shelf from January to March, and black marlin push in to the Big Gibber when the fish arrive. Tuna take over wide of the port from about April to July, while reef and estuary fishing runs all year.

p: Port Stephens pairs a large, sheltered estuary with quick access to offshore islands and the continental shelf. Reef boats leave through Tomaree and Yacaaba heads for Cabbage Tree, Boondelbah, Little and Broughton islands, while game boats fish the FADs about 20 km out, the Big Gibber to the north and the shelf beyond.

p: Port Stephens is about 2.5 hours' drive north of Sydney. Some reef charters set a minimum age of 12, while others run sheltered kids' sessions, so match the trip to your group.
The waterway is a marine park, and estuary guides explain the park and its wildlife on the trip. Several Port Stephens charters include NSW fishing licences for their guests.

faq: Can you catch all three marlin species in one day at Port Stephens?
It's possible. Port Stephens is one of the few places where blue, black and striped marlin can all be encountered, and game crews chase a single-day grand slam in summer.
What can you catch inside Port Stephens without going offshore?

Depending on the month, the estuary holds bream, flathead, whiting, luderick, mulloway, tailor, salmon, kingfish, squid and even longtail tuna. The Myall, Karuah and Tilligerry tributaries give shelter when the bay is choppy.
How far out are the marlin grounds from Port Stephens?
Light-tackle boats run about 20 km to the FAD region or north to the Big Gibber. Blue marlin trips go out over the continental shelf.
Are there kids' fishing charters in Port Stephens?
Yes. Options include a two-hour estuary trip for under-10s and a 3.5-hour family morning in sheltered water near Cabbage Tree Island or Fingal.
Is there a short estuary fishing trip in Port Stephens?

Yes. Hammerhead Fishing Charters runs a three-hour estuary experience inside Port Stephens for up to six people ($780, extra people $95 each), and a dedicated estuary guide offers five-hour dawn or dusk lure sessions and two-hour kids' trips.

intro: Port Macquarie combines offshore reef fishing with some of the best estuary lure fishing on the Mid North Coast. Deep sea boats leave the Town Green boardwalk at dawn for six-hour trips to the offshore reefs, chasing snapper, pearl perch, kingfish, flathead and jewfish, with mahi mahi in the warmer months.

The Hastings River is tidal for about 32 km inland, and private lure guides also fish the Maria, Macleay and Manning rivers for dusky flathead, mulloway, bream and whiting, plus catch-and-release Australian bass from September to May. Humpback whales are often seen from offshore boats during the migration.
port-macquarie.season: There is something to catch all year. Dusky flathead and mulloway are year-round estuary targets, whiting work the sand flats from about October to April, and guided Australian bass trips run September to May. Offshore, spring and summer are the main seasons for snapper and reef fish, with mahi mahi in the warmer months.

p: Port Macquarie charters split between offshore reef trips from the town centre and guided lure fishing on the region's rivers. The Hastings River, a NSW Recreational Fishing Haven, is tidal for about 32 km to just upstream of Wauchope, and guides also travel to the Maria, Macleay and Manning rivers.

Flathead, bream, whiting and mulloway

p: Humpback whales are often seen from offshore charters during the migration. On guided estuary trips Australian bass are released, and at least one guide can't clean fish on board, so bring a bucket or cooler.
Families who just want to throw a line in can fish the town wharf, the Settlement Point picnic area or the southern breakwall.

faq: How far up the Hastings River can you fish?
The Hastings is tidal for about 32 km inland, to just upstream of Wauchope. Most anglers fish the estuary and lower reaches, with freshwater bass in the upper river.
Can you fish for Australian bass near Port Macquarie?
Yes. Guided bass trips run from September to May on the Maria River, about 20 minutes from Port Macquarie, or the Macleay, about 40 minutes away. Bass are catch and release.
Where can families fish without a boat in Port Macquarie?

The town wharf and the wharves beside the Short Street charter berth suit families. Settlement Point picnic area produces whiting, bream and flathead, and the southern breakwall holds tailor, bream, mulloway and luderick.

intro: South West Rocks, roughly halfway between Sydney and Brisbane, has unusually quick access to good water. The first ocean reef is about ten minutes from the Macleay River bar, most fishing is done 1 to 5 km out, and the continental shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, so the East Australian Current can push marlin, wahoo and mahi mahi close to shore.

Fish Rock, Green Island and the Gaol Grounds off Smoky Cape are the best-known spots, with reefs running from Nambucca Heads to Hungry Head. When it's rough outside, the Macleay River estuary holds flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting and mangrove jack.
south-west-rocks.season: As a rough guide, warm-water species such as mackerel run from about January to May and cool-water species such as snapper and kingfish from May to December. Black marlin turn up from early summer to late autumn, often close in, striped marlin peak in spring, large yellowfin sit on the shelf in winter and spring, and mahi mahi are best in November and December.

p: South West Rocks has unusually quick access to deep water. The first ocean reef is about ten minutes from the bar, most fishing is 1–5 km out, and the continental shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, so the East Australian Current can push warm water right up to the rocks.
items: Fish Rock
Rises from about 30 m of water off Smoky Cape; resident kingfish all year. Marine-park zone: no bait fishing within 200 m
Green Island and Black Rock

p: Fish Rock and Green Island are marine-park zones protecting grey nurse sharks: no bait fishing within 200 m, though lures are allowed. Trips cross the Macleay River bar; operators reschedule for strong wind or big seas, but usually not for rain.
South West Rocks sits roughly halfway between Sydney and Brisbane on the Mid North Coast, and fishing-and-accommodation packages are available for groups.

faq: Can you fish with bait at Fish Rock?
No. Fish Rock and Green Island are marine-park zones protecting grey nurse sharks, so bait fishing isn't allowed within 200 m. Lures are fine.
How far offshore is the continental shelf at South West Rocks?
Only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, one of its closest points to the east coast. That is why marlin, wahoo and mahi mahi can turn up very close to shore.
What happens if it's too rough to fish offshore at South West Rocks?
Guides can switch to the Macleay River estuary, which holds flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting, trevally and mangrove jack and stays fishable when the sea isn't.

intro: Yamba and Iluka sit either side of the Clarence River mouth on the NSW North Coast. Charters cross the Clarence River bar to reefs 5 to 10 km out, choosing from more than 20 spots on the day, and the larger boat ranges from Evans Head to Sandon and out towards the continental shelf.

Snapper and pearl perch are the main reef targets, with flathead and mulloway on the bottom and kingfish, mackerel, tailor and salmon on lures when surface fish show. Both operators pick up from Iluka on request, and one also runs humpback whale cruises between Woody Head and Angourie.
yamba.season: Morning reef trips run seven days a week in every season, weather permitting, for snapper, pearl perch, flathead and mulloway. Lures are run for kingfish, mackerel, tailor and salmon when surface fish appear, and humpback whale cruises operate during the migration.

Most reef trips fish 5–10 km off the Clarence River bar, choosing from more than 20 spots on the day. The larger boat ranges from Evans Head to Sandon and out towards the continental shelf.
Can you get picked up from Iluka for a Yamba fishing charter?

Do Yamba fishing charters cross the Clarence River bar?

intro: Charters on this stretch of the far North Coast leave from Brunswick Heads, about 15 minutes north of Byron Bay, and Evans Head, between Ballina and Yamba. Brunswick Heads boats fish the reefs off Byron for snapper, pearl perch, jewfish and kingfish and chase marlin, tuna, mackerel and wahoo wider out.

Evans Head specialises in deep-water pearl perch and snapper in about 80 m, roughly 30 km offshore, and sells week-long midweek fishing-and-accommodation packages. In March 2026 NSW DPI also deployed a new offshore artificial reef 5 km south of the Richmond River mouth off Ballina.
ballina-byron.season: Pearl perch and snapper are caught year-round on the deep reefs off Evans Head and Byron. The warmer months add mackerel, wahoo, tuna and marlin, and humpback whales pass close by from about May to July heading north and September to November heading south.

intro: Lord Howe Island sits on the world's southernmost coral reef, where the East Australian Current pushes deep water up the island's slopes and tropical and temperate fish share the same water. Its kingfish are famously large, and the surrounding marine park has no commercial fishery.

Charters leave the lagoon jetty, with departure times set around the tides. Shared and private trips fish the island shelf and reef edges, while longer days run about 23 km to Balls Pyramid, the world's tallest sea stack, for kingfish, yellowfin and wahoo. Boats are small (Sea Buoys takes four anglers at most), so book early in your stay.
lord-howe-island.season: Kingfish are caught year-round, and winter is the best of it, which runs against the summer visitor season. Yellowfin tuna and wahoo are offshore targets in season, marlin are a lightly fished option, and summer brings calmer water and long evenings for sight-casting in the lagoon.

p: The waters are a marine park: spearfishing is banned, bag limits apply to bluefish and double headers, and catch and release is encouraged. Sharks take hooked fish fairly often, so expect to lose a few.
Flights to the island are weather-affected more often than most, so book fishing early in your stay to leave room to reschedule, and consider travel insurance. Phone reception offshore is unreliable.

faq: How far is Balls Pyramid from Lord Howe Island?
About 23 km. The 552 m sea stack is the world's tallest, and charters run five-hour shared or sole-use trips to fish around it, as well as full-day offshore trips.
Why do Lord Howe fishing charter times change each day?
Boats leave from the jetty inside the lagoon and can't get out on a very low tide (one operator's limit is about 0.3 m), so departure times shift with the tides through the week.
Can you spearfish at Lord Howe Island?
No. Spearfishing is banned in the Lord Howe Island Marine Park, and bag limits apply to some lagoon species such as bluefish and double header.
What is the Lord Howe lagoon grand slam?

Catching a trevally, silver drummer, bluefish and the endemic double header wrasse in one session of sight-casting in the shallow lagoon. Bag limits apply to bluefish and double headers, and catch and release is encouraged.

intro: Sydney is one of the few big cities where you can catch kingfish, jewfish (mulloway) and snapper within sight of the Opera House. Harbour guides work the headlands, bays and moorings of Port Jackson, Middle Harbour and Pittwater, while offshore boats run out through the Heads, or from Cronulla and Port Botany, to reefs 1 to 12 nautical miles out and to the FADs and the shelf for mahi mahi, tuna and marlin.

Charters leave from Rose Bay, Watsons Bay, Manly Wharf, Thames Street Wharf at Balmain, The Spit, Cronulla and Port Botany, and several harbour boats collect groups from public wharves. Shared reef seats start at about $200, private harbour and reef boats at about $1,200, and full-day game boats cost roughly $2,200 to $3,300.
sydney.season: There is fishing off Sydney all year. Kingfish are caught year-round but peak from spring into early summer, and jewfish fire in the harbour from October to July. Summer brings mahi mahi to the FADs and black marlin from around Christmas, with blue marlin best late in summer and into autumn. Winter is the time for yellowfin and albacore tuna, gemfish, blue-eye trevalla and snapper on the inshore reefs.

p: Sydney charters split into harbour trips and offshore trips. Harbour guides fish Sydney Harbour itself for kingfish and jewfish, often within sight of the Opera House, while offshore boats run out through the Heads, or from Cronulla and Port Botany in the south, to reefs roughly 1 to 12 nautical miles out in 30 to 120 m of water. Sport and game boats troll the named reefs and the NSW DPI fish aggregating devices (FADs) for kingfish, mahi mahi, tuna and marlin.

Several offshore operators say they will not return early for seasickness, so take a preventative if you are prone to it. Age limits vary: Sydney Charter Fishing does not take children under eight, and Sydney Premium Charters' shared and mahi mahi trips are for ages 12 and up, while its private trips have no age limit.

faq: Can you catch kingfish in Sydney Harbour?
Yes. Kingfish are a year-round option in Sydney Harbour, and fish over a metre are not uncommon. Harbour guides use live squid and stickbait lures, and the best run is from spring into early summer.
Can I join a Sydney fishing charter on my own?

Yes. Shared seats are sold by Deep Blue Charters at Rose Bay ($200 half-day reef), Sydney Charter Fishing at Manly ($240-$280), Sydney Premium Charters at Cronulla on weekends ($260) and Cronulla Reef Fishing Charters ($250 for a full day). Some shared trips need a minimum number of anglers to run.
When is marlin season off Sydney?

Mainly summer and autumn. Small black marlin turn up on the inshore reefs from around Christmas, striped marlin peak in summer, and blue marlin are most likely late in summer and into autumn, when the biggest fish are caught. Striped marlin are occasionally caught in winter too.
How far offshore do Sydney reef fishing trips go?

Most reef trips fish between about 1 and 12 nautical miles off the coast in 30 to 120 m of water. Mahi mahi trips run about 20 km offshore to the FADs, and deep-drop trips go further out to Browns Mountain.
Can a big group go fishing together in Sydney?

Yes. Deep Blue Charters' Mystery Bay takes up to 28 people with 18 fishing on a half day, and its other two boats take 23 to 25. Blue Reef Fishing Charters fishes up to 14 offshore on Strike Back, and Sydney Charter Fishing takes private groups of up to 14.

intro: Wollongong and Kiama put you on the Illawarra's reefs within minutes of leaving harbour. Boats from Belmore Basin in Wollongong Harbour drift reefs from Stanwell Park to Shellharbour for snapper, morwong, flathead and pigfish, while Kiama's boat is in open ocean almost as soon as it clears Robertson Basin, with reefs within 15 km and the continental shelf about 30 km out.

Game boats chase marlin, mahi mahi and mako sharks from December to April and tuna from June to October, and Kiama runs cool-season deep-drop trips in up to 400 m of water for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku. Big shared boats make this a good choice for solo anglers and mixed groups.
wollongong.season: Reef fishing for snapper, morwong, flathead and pigfish runs all year. Game boats chase marlin, mahi mahi, mako sharks, yellowfin and wahoo from December to April, then yellowfin, bluefin and albacore tuna from June to October. Deep-sea trips to the shelf for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku run in the cooler months, roughly May to September.

From Kiama the boat is in open ocean almost as soon as it leaves the harbour, with reef grounds within about 15 km and the continental shelf about 30 km offshore for deep-water and game fishing.

How far out is the continental shelf from Kiama?
About 30 km. Kiama Charter Service's deep sea trips fish the shelf in water up to 400 m deep for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku, mainly from May to September, and you can still see land.
Are there fishing trips for kids in Wollongong?
Yes. Aquilla Fishing Charters runs two-hour Junior Angler school-holiday sessions for kids aged 8 to 16, with a supervising adult included in the booking. Dates are posted on its social media.
Can I join a shared fishing trip in Wollongong?

Yes. Aquilla Fishing Charters sells seats on its 60 ft boat for $225 (minimum seven to run), Five Island Charters runs reef charters at $200 a head with a minimum of four, and Kiama Charter Service charges $205 per person for reef days, also with a minimum of four.

intro: Jervis Bay pairs a sheltered, clear-water bay with deep water and the continental shelf close by. The bay is renowned for squid over the seagrass edges and good bottom fishing for snapper, and charters head outside to the reefs for snapper, morwong, flathead and gummy sharks.

Further out, game and deep-water trips chase kingfish, yellowfin tuna, marlin and sharks, or blue-eye trevalla, hapuku and gemfish. JB Fishing Charters sells per-person seats for a full day out of Jervis Bay, and Escape Fishing Charters runs groups of up to 12 from Greenwell Point, 20 minutes north. The bay is a marine park, so zoning rules apply.
jervis-bay.season: Squid and snapper are caught through much of the year in the bay and on the offshore reefs, along with morwong and flathead. The warmer months bring pelagics such as mahi mahi and tuna, and the area is known for marlin over summer and autumn.

p: Jervis Bay is a marine park with sheltered water inside the bay and deep water right outside it, and the continental shelf is close by. Charters fish the reefs off the bay and the Shoalhaven coast for table fish, and head wider for pelagics and deep-water species.

intro: Three charter ports cover this part of the NSW South Coast. Batemans Bay boats leave d'Albora Marina to fish the reefs in and around the bay and the Tollgate Islands for snapper, kingfish, morwong and flathead, and run about 22 km out to the continental shelf for game fish and deep dropping.

Narooma's town wharf is the closest port to Barunguba (Montague Island), about 9 km offshore and a well-known reef and game fishing area. Further south, Bermagui boats leave O'Shea Wharf for reef fish, kingfish, yellowfin tuna, sharks and deep-water gemfish and blue-eye trevalla. All three operators include licence cover.
batemans-bay.season: Reef fish such as snapper, morwong, flathead and kingfish are caught all year around Montague Island and the Batemans Bay reefs. The offshore game season runs from about December to June: marlin from around Christmas until the water cools in June, and yellowfin and albacore tuna best in late autumn.

p: Three ports cover this stretch of the South Coast. Batemans Bay boats fish the reefs in and around the bay and run about 22 km out to the continental shelf for game fish and deep-drop fishing. Narooma boats work the reefs between the town and Barunguba (Montague Island), about 9 km offshore, and the shelf roughly 20 km out. Further south, Bermagui boats fish for reef fish, kingfish, yellowfin tuna, sharks and deep-water table fish.

Game On Charters says the shelf is about 22 km from the Batemans Bay marina. Off Narooma it is around 20 km out, with Montague Island roughly halfway.
When is marlin season on the South Coast near Narooma?

Narooma Charters puts the game season at December to June. Striped and black marlin are around from about Christmas until the water cools in June, and yellowfin and albacore tuna are best in late autumn.
Can you go deep-drop fishing from Batemans Bay or Bermagui?

Yes. Game On Charters runs full-day shared or private deep-drop trips from Batemans Bay with Shimano electric reels, and FishBermi in Bermagui offers trips for deep-water table fish such as gemfish and blue-eye trevalla.

intro: On the far South Coast, Eden's Twofold Bay is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Southern Hemisphere and has no bar to cross, so boats can get out in conditions that close other ports. Eden charters fish the inshore reefs for snapper, morwong and flathead year-round, run south to 'kingie country', and head about 19 nautical miles to the continental shelf for game fish.

Merimbula, 30 minutes north, adds three- to five-hour reef trips from Mitchies Jetty and the town jetty, plus calm lake fishing for dusky flathead and bream in Merimbula and Pambula lakes. Both towns are whale-watching hubs during the humpback migration, and Merimbula's airport has daily flights to Sydney and Melbourne.
eden.season: Snapper and flathead are caught year-round. Wider reef trips for morwong, ocean perch and shark run February to April, kingfish from about November to June, and Eden's game season for marlin, yellowfin, albacore and striped tuna from November to the end of July, with January to late March often best for marlin. Merimbula's three-hour reef charter runs December to July.

p: Eden boats work Twofold Bay and the inshore reefs for snapper, morwong, leatherjackets and flathead, run a few minutes south to the kingfish grounds around Mowarry Point and Green Cape, and head out to the continental shelf for game fish. Merimbula operators fish the local reefs off Merimbula Bay on shorter trips, while the sheltered lakes offer calm-water flathead fishing.

Snapper, morwong, leatherjackets and flathead all year; wider reef trips in February to April add ocean perch and shark
Mowarry Point and Green Cape
'Kingie country' south of Eden; Mowarry is about 10 minutes from port
The continental shelf off Twofold Bay
Most game catches come around the shelf, about 19 nautical miles out, in 50 to 70 fathoms
Merimbula reefs
Snapper, kingfish, morwong, tiger and sand flathead, trevally, nannygai and leatherjacket
Merimbula and Pambula lakes
Dusky flathead are the main target, with bream, luderick, trevally and whiting

p: Reef fishing runs all year out of Eden. The warmer months bring kingfish and the long game season, and Merimbula's short reef charter runs over the warmer half of the year.

Year-round; snapper are caught on almost every Eden reef trip
Morwong, ocean perch and shark (wider reefs)
February to April
Kingfish
About November to June; most fish 5 to 8 kg, up to around 15 kg
Marlin, yellowfin, albacore and striped tuna, broadbill
Game season November to the end of July; January to late March is often best for marlin
Eden Harbour (Snug Cove)
Home of Eden's charter boats; the harbour has no bar to cross

Departure point for Fishpen Charters, on Merimbula Lake

Departure point for Sapphire Coastal Adventures' three-hour reef charter

Four-lane public ramp with fish tables, washdown bay and parking

p: Merimbula is about 454 km south of Sydney on the Princes Highway and 243 km from Canberra, and Merimbula Regional Airport has daily Rex and Qantas connections to Sydney and Melbourne. Eden is about 30 minutes' drive further south.

Humpback whales pass close to shore during the May to November migration, and boats must keep at least 100 m from adult whales. Twofold Bay has an active Navy wharf, and exclusion zones apply when Navy ships are alongside. Charters that include licence cover mean you do not need your own NSW recreational fishing licence on board.

faq: Does Eden have a bar crossing?
No. Visit Eden describes Twofold Bay as the Southern Hemisphere's third-deepest harbour, with no bar to cross, so Eden charters can head out in conditions that keep bar ports closed.
When is the game fishing season at Eden?

Visit Eden puts the main game season at November to the end of July, with marlin, yellowfin, albacore and striped tuna, sharks and broadbill. Trade-A-Boat notes January to late March often fishes best for marlin.
When are the kingfish around Eden?
Freedom Charters runs its kingfish-focused sports trips from about November to June in 'kingie country' south of Eden, where most fish are 5 to 8 kg.
Is there a short fishing trip for families at Merimbula?
Yes. Sapphire Coastal Adventures runs a three-hour reef charter from the Merimbula Public Jetty, and Fishpen Charters runs three-hour trips from Mitchies Jetty that are popular with families.
How far is Merimbula from Sydney and Canberra?

Merimbula is about 454 km south of Sydney on the Princes Highway and 243 km from Canberra. Merimbula Regional Airport has daily Rex and Qantas flights to Sydney and Melbourne, and Eden is a further 30 minutes south.

intro: New South Wales charters run the length of the coast, from Tweed Heads on the Queensland border to Eden near Victoria, plus Lord Howe Island far out in the Tasman Sea. Warm water carried south by the East Australian Current brings marlin, mahi mahi and tuna to most ports in summer and autumn, while snapper, kingfish, flathead and jewfish (mulloway) are caught all year.

Sydney has the most choice, from harbour guides chasing kingfish and jewfish to offshore reef and game boats. Port Stephens is the state's best-known marlin port, the North Coast mixes reef fishing for snapper and pearl perch with summer mackerel, and the South Coast from Wollongong to Eden has deep water close to shore, island reefs and a long game season. Half-day reef and estuary trips suit families; full-day offshore and game charters suit experienced anglers.
new-south-wales.season: Reef fishing for snapper, morwong and flathead runs all year along most of the coast. Game fishing peaks in summer and early autumn, roughly December to April from the Tweed to Wollongong, and runs later in the south: to about June off Narooma and from November to July at Eden. In the cooler months southern boats deep-drop the shelf for blue-eye trevalla and gemfish.

sections.h: Fishing regions along the NSW coast
p: NSW charters fall into a few broad regions. On the North Coast, where tropical and temperate currents meet, reef trips for snapper and pearl perch mix with mackerel, mahi mahi and marlin. Port Stephens, Newcastle and the Central Coast pair big estuaries and lakes with offshore reefs and a strong marlin season. Sydney and the Illawarra offer harbour, reef and shelf fishing close to the city, and the South Coast has deep water close to shore, island reefs and a long game season.
items: Tweed, Byron, Yamba and Coffs Harbour
Snapper and pearl perch on the reefs, with mackerel, mahi mahi and marlin in summer; Coffs sits beside the Solitary Islands Marine Park
South West Rocks and Port Macquarie
The shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off South West Rocks; estuary trips on the Hastings and Macleay rivers
Port Stephens, Newcastle and Lake Macquarie
Black, striped and blue marlin off Port Stephens; flathead, bream and mulloway in Lake Macquarie and the Hunter
Sydney and the Central Coast
Kingfish and jewfish in Sydney Harbour, snapper on the offshore reefs and mahi mahi at the FADs
Wollongong, Kiama and Jervis Bay
Reef drifts for snapper and morwong, deep-drop trips at the shelf, and squid in Jervis Bay
Batemans Bay to Eden
Montague Island and Batemans Bay reefs, kingfish south of Eden, and Eden's game season from November to July
Lord Howe Island
Large kingfish year-round, with yellowfin and wahoo offshore and Balls Pyramid about 23 km away

p: Bottom fishing for snapper, morwong and flathead runs all year along most of the coast. Summer and early autumn are the main game-fishing months, when warm currents bring marlin and mahi mahi within reach, and the season runs later the further south you go. In the cooler months, southern boats run deep-drop trips for blue-eye trevalla, gemfish and hapuku, and yellowfin and albacore tuna turn up off Sydney and the South Coast.
items: Marlin
About December to April from Tweed Heads to Wollongong; off Narooma to June, and Eden's game season runs November to July
Mahi mahi
Summer, around the fish aggregating devices (FADs)
Kingfish
Year-round in Sydney Harbour; about November to June south of Eden
Snapper
Year-round on the reefs; winter and spring are strongest on the North Coast
Deep-water species (blue-eye, gemfish, hapuku)
Cooler months: May to September off Kiama, and July to August at Browns Mountain off Sydney

p: Many NSW charters include licence cover for their passengers, but not all do: Reel Adventure Fishing in Sydney asks every angler to buy their own NSW recreational fishing licence, so check before you go. Several stretches of coast are marine parks with zoning rules, including Cape Byron, the Solitary Islands, Port Stephens-Great Lakes, Jervis Bay, Batemans and Lord Howe Island. NSW DPI recommends checking the zoning map or the FishSmart app; charter skippers know the boundaries, and the operator's licence covers you on a licensed charter boat.
Prices below are examples from current operator price lists; check the listing for each trip's inclusions and minimum numbers.

About $200-$260 per person for five to eight hours, e.g. Deep Blue Charters (Rose Bay), Port Macquarie Fishing Charters, Evans Head and Five Island Charters
Private reef charter (whole boat)
From about $1,200 for a small Sydney boat to $3,600 for a 60 ft Wollongong boat carrying 22

From $1,800 for four anglers at South West Rocks to $3,300 for six on a Sydney game boat

From $470 for one angler on a half day on the Hastings River at Port Macquarie

Short sheltered-water trips in Port Stephens, Wollongong and Newcastle, from $89 per child

faq: Where can you catch marlin in NSW?

Marlin are targeted from Tweed Heads to Eden. Port Stephens is one of the few places where black, striped and blue marlin can be caught on the same day, Sydney boats chase them through summer and autumn, and Eden's game season runs from November to the end of July.
Are there marine parks on the NSW coast?

Yes. They include Cape Byron, the Solitary Islands (the oldest marine park in NSW), Jervis Bay, Batemans and Lord Howe Island. Each has zoning rules about where and how you can fish, which charter skippers follow. NSW DPI's FishSmart app shows the zones.
Where can you go deep-drop fishing in NSW?

Kiama Charter Service runs deep sea trips to the shelf about 30 km out, in water up to 400 m, from May to September. Batemans Bay and Bermagui boats also fish deep water for blue-eye trevalla and gemfish, and Sydney boats drop on Browns Mountain in winter.
Where can you catch big kingfish in NSW?

Kingfish are caught year-round in Sydney Harbour, Fish Rock off South West Rocks holds resident kingfish, and Coffs Harbour boats target them around South Solitary Island. Lord Howe Island is known for very large kingfish, best in winter, and Eden's kingfish run from about November to June.
Is winter a good time for a fishing charter in NSW?

Yes, for the right targets. Reef fishing runs all year, yellowfin and albacore tuna turn up off Sydney and the Illawarra from about June to October, Kiama runs deep-sea trips to the shelf from May to September, and Lord Howe's kingfish are best in winter.

darwin.summary: Darwin fishing charters leave Cullen Bay, Stokes Hill Wharf and the Dinah Beach ramp, while barra guides collect guests from hotels. Harbour trips target barramundi, golden snapper, black jewfish and mud crabs year-round; offshore reefs 20–50 km out add Spanish mackerel and tuna in the dry. Shared half days start at about $225 per person; private full days cost $1,900–$3,540.
intro: Darwin puts you within reach of both world-class barramundi water and productive offshore reefs. Harbour and estuary charters fish the creeks and mangroves around Darwin Harbour for barra, mangrove jack and threadfin salmon, while bluewater trips head offshore for Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, golden trevally, longtail tuna and sailfish.

Most charters leave from Cullen Bay, Stokes Hill Wharf or the Dinah Beach ramp, and offshore trips work reefs such as Fish Reef, Lorna Shoals and Charles Point, roughly 20–50km out. Tides here often run six to seven metres, which shapes where and when guides fish. Several operators also run day trips to Shoal Bay, Bynoe Harbour, the Adelaide River and Corroboree Billabong.
darwin.season: Golden snapper and black jewfish are caught year-round, and barramundi are in Darwin Harbour all year, with the run-off (roughly March to May) the classic barra window. The dry season (about May to August) is best for trevally, queenfish, mackerel and tuna, while sailfish and marlin show up in the tropical summer.

p: Darwin sits on a peninsula with Darwin Harbour to the west, the Timor Sea to the north and Shoal Bay to the east, so guides can usually find a sheltered launch whatever the wind. The harbour itself is many times the size of Sydney Harbour, with three main arms full of mangrove creeks, and its Second World War and Cyclone Tracy wrecks hold black jewfish.

Half-day trips mostly stay inside the harbour. Full-day and extended bluewater trips run out to reefs 20–50 km offshore, while barra guides drive clients to Shoal Bay, Bynoe Harbour, the Adelaide River or the Mary River billabongs.
items: Darwin Harbour
Barramundi in the creeks and arms, golden snapper and black jewfish on rock, reef and wrecks, plus mud crabs; most half-day trips fish here
Fish Reef, Middle Reef, Bass Reef and Lorna Shoals
Offshore reef grounds about 20–50 km out, fished on 8–10 hour bluewater days for jewfish, golden snapper and Spanish mackerel
Shoal Bay and the Howard River
North-east of Darwin; big barra at 'the rock' in the build-up and good mud crabbing, but the bay dries into sandbars at low tide
Bynoe Harbour
Under two hours' drive south-west; mangrove creeks for barra, threadfin salmon and mangrove jack, deep holes for jewfish
Adelaide River
About 70 km east of Darwin; creek mouths fish for barra in the build-up and run-off, with jewfish and golden snapper near the mouth
Corroboree Billabong and Shady Camp (Mary River)
Barra and saratoga day trips with early hotel pick-up, run by several Darwin operators
Vernon Islands and Tiwi Islands
Reef and pelagic grounds reached by fast boats from Darwin or from Leaders Creek

p: Darwin fishes all year, but the target changes with the season and the tide. Reef fish are a constant, pelagics peak in the dry, and calm build-up days open up billfish.
items: Black jewfish and golden snapper
Practically year-round on the reefs and wrecks
Spanish mackerel and longtail tuna
Through the dry season
Sailfish and marlin
The calm months of October to December; billfish trips are usually catch and release
Barramundi
All year in Darwin Harbour; the run-off (about March–May) and the build-up are the big-fish windows
Mud crabs
Harbour, Shoal Bay and Bynoe creeks; several operators add crabbing when tides suit
Cullen Bay Ferry Terminal
Bluewater reef charters such as Equinox and Yknot; times are set by the tide
Stokes Hill Wharf (Dock 2)
Harbour charters with Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters; car park on the left as you enter the wharf
Dinah Beach boat ramp, Stuart Park
At the end of Gonzales Road, Stuart Park; used by Offshore Boats, River & Reef, Obsession and Alure (harbour trips meet at 6:45am for a 7am start)
Leaders Creek boat ramp
About an hour from Darwin, with secure parking; the closest ramp to the Tiwi Islands

p: Tides of 6–7 metres are common, so departure times and fishing spots move with the tide; confirm your start time when you book. Saltwater crocodiles live in the harbour and creeks, so stay back from the water's edge at ramps and never swim. Sandflies are common at ramps and in the harbour mangroves: long light pants, socks and repellent help.

Bag and size limits apply to most species, so check the current NT Fisheries rules or the free NT Fishing Mate app before keeping fish. The annual Million Dollar Fish competition releases tagged barramundi across the Top End each season, and several Darwin operators promote it.

faq: Do Darwin fishing charters pick you up from your hotel?

Barra day tours usually do: operators such as Barra Private Tours, DNA Barra Fishing, Obsession and River & Reef collect guests around 4:30–5am. Harbour and bluewater trips generally meet at the wharf or ramp (Stokes Hill Wharf, Cullen Bay or Dinah Beach). Barra or Blue charges $50 per person for return transfers.
Should I choose a harbour trip or an offshore reef trip in Darwin?

Harbour half days stay within about 20 minutes of the wharf or ramp for barra, golden snapper, jewfish and mud crabs, and suit families and calm-water anglers. Offshore days of 8–10 hours run 20–50 km out to Fish Reef, Lorna Shoals and nearby grounds for bigger jewfish, golden snapper, coral trout and Spanish mackerel, but depend on wind and tides.
Can you do a Mary River barra trip as a day trip from Darwin?

Yes. Corroboree Billabong, part of the Mary River system, is about 1.5 hours' drive from Darwin, and several Darwin operators run full-day billabong trips with pre-dawn hotel pick-up, returning mid to late afternoon. Shady Camp is further, about two hours or more.
How big are the tides in Darwin?
Tides of 6–7 metres are common, which strongly affects where and when charters fish. Local boats are built to handle them, and departure times are set around the tide rather than a fixed schedule.
Can I take my fish home on the plane from Darwin?

Often, yes. Several operators fillet and bag the catch, and some, such as Offshore Boats, will freeze and pack it in airline-approved seafood boxes on request. Otherwise bring an esky or insulated cooler bag, and keep within NT possession limits.
Is a Darwin Harbour fishing trip suitable for young children?

Often, yes. Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters sells a family charter for two adults and three children, Barra Private Tours takes guests from age 5 on its half and full days, and Alure's 7-hour harbour trip (ages 8+) is back at the ramp by about 2pm. Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters' boats have no toilet on board, so ask about facilities when you book.
Can I book a Darwin fishing charter on my own?

Yes, on shared trips priced per person, but check minimums. Equinox needs at least four passengers for any charter to run, Obsession needs two but will look for spare seats on other bookings, and Barra Private Tours' shared half days need three guests, so solo anglers should ask before paying.

kakadu.summary: Kakadu fishing charters are run by a few park-licensed guides. Kakadu Fishing Tours collects guests in Jabiru, about 2.5 hours from Darwin, for short dry-season barra sessions (June–October) on the East Alligator above Cahill's Crossing, and DNA Barra Fishing drives run-off guests from Darwin to the Alligator rivers (March–May). Run-off full days cost $2,380 per boat for up to four.
intro: Kakadu National Park, about two and a half hours from Darwin, offers barramundi fishing in a world-heritage landscape: the big tidal South and East Alligator rivers, the Yellow Water floodplain and, beneath the Arnhem Land escarpment, the upper East Alligator above Cahill's Crossing.

Guided fishing inside the park is limited to a small number of operators that meet the park's criteria, and trips generally run from Jabiru. On smaller tides, guides may also head to the reefs off the river mouths for golden snapper and black jewfish.
kakadu.season: The run-off, from about March to May, is prime time on the big tidal rivers. Through the dry season (around June to October) the upper East Alligator fishes well, and some barramundi fishing continues at Yellow Water over the wet, when most operators close.

p: Only licensed guides who meet the park's criteria may run fishing tours inside Kakadu National Park, and both operators listed here are approved. Trips work the big tidal Alligator rivers in the run-off and the scenic upper East Alligator in the dry season.
items: East Alligator River above Cahill's Crossing
Dry-season trips beside the Arnhem Land escarpment, where freshwater and saltwater barramundi are caught; Kakadu Fishing Tours' record there is 135 cm
South and East Alligator rivers
Big tidal rivers fished on full-day and extended trips during the March–May run-off
Reefs off the Alligator river mouths
Golden snapper and black jewfish on the smaller tides during run-off trips
Yellow Water (South Alligator floodplain)
Has a boat ramp and holds barramundi; NT tourism notes it can still be fished in the wet season when most operators close
Run-off (March to early May)
Prime time for trophy barra on the tidal rivers; Kakadu Fishing Tours and DNA Barra Fishing run full-day and multi-day charters
Dry season (June to October)
Short morning, midday and afternoon barra sessions on the upper East Alligator from Jabiru
Tropical summer (wet season)
Most fishing operators close; flooding can shut parts of the park, so check the Kakadu Access Report

p: Jabiru is about a 2.5-hour drive from Darwin. Kakadu Fishing Tours picks up from Jabiru accommodation, while DNA Barra Fishing collects run-off guests in Darwin and drives them in by 4WD, with accommodation at the Crocodile Hotel or Anbinik Resort in Jabiru.
items: Jabiru
Base for both operators' Kakadu trips; accommodation pick-up
Darwin
Pick-up for DNA Barra Fishing's 2–14 day run-off trips
Bowali Visitor Centre, Jabiru
Check river conditions and the daily access report if launching your own boat; passes can be bought here too

p: A Kakadu park pass, sold by Parks Australia, is valid for 7 days and covers Kakadu only; NT residents are free. An adult pass is $40 in the dry season (15 May to 31 October) and $25 in the tropical summer, and Parks Australia says passes for visits between 1 July and 31 October 2026 are charged at wet-season rates. Guided tours may include entry permits, so ask your operator.

Parks Australia says Kakadu has the same fishing bag limits as the Mary and Daly rivers, asks anglers to fish only in the areas set aside for visitors and to practise catch and release, and advises land-based anglers to stand at least 5 metres back from the bank. Saltwater crocodiles are in every Kakadu waterway. Weather can change quickly, so check the access report and the Bureau of Meteorology radar, and keep your trip flexible.

faq: Which fishing guides can operate inside Kakadu National Park?

Only licensed operators who meet the park's criteria. DNA Barra Fishing says it is one of the few guides approved to fish the park, and Kakadu Fishing Tours describes itself as one of a select few operators and the only one based full time in Kakadu.
How far is Kakadu from Darwin for a fishing trip?
Jabiru, the base for Kakadu fishing tours, is about a 2.5-hour drive from Darwin. Because of the travel time, DNA Barra Fishing's Kakadu trips run for two days or more.
Can you fish Kakadu in the wet season?

Most fishing operators close during the tropical summer, but NT tourism notes you can still fish Yellow Water on the South Alligator floodplain, which has a boat ramp. The park is open all year, though flooding closes some areas, so check the Kakadu Access Report.
Can you catch saltwater barra at Cahill's Crossing?

Above the crossing, yes: Kakadu Fishing Tours fishes the East Alligator just upstream, where both freshwater and saltwater barramundi are caught. Saltwater crocodiles share the river, so fish from the boat with your guide.
How long are dry-season fishing trips in Kakadu?

Short. From June to October Kakadu Fishing Tours runs three sessions a day on the upper East Alligator, roughly 6:30–10:30am, 10:45am–1:45pm and 2–6pm, with pick-up from Jabiru accommodation. Run-off charters in March to early May are full days, and DNA's Kakadu trips last two days or more.
Do I need a park pass to go fishing in Kakadu?

Yes. Everyone except NT residents needs a Kakadu park pass from Parks Australia, valid for 7 days; an adult pass is $40 in the dry season and $25 in the tropical summer. No fishing licence is needed, but Kakadu uses the same bag limits as the Mary and Daly rivers. Ask your guide whether the pass is included.

daly-river.summary: Daly River fishing charters launch from the Daly River (Nauiyu) ramp, about 2.5 hours south-west of Darwin, for barramundi, mangrove jack and threadfin salmon. NT Fish & 4x4 runs half and full days from $380 per person and a $650 Big Day Out to Anson Bay; Humbug Fishing runs 5–7 day motherships from Darwin. The March–May run-off is peak season.
intro: The Daly River, about 210–220km south-west of Darwin, is one of the Territory's great barramundi rivers — and it's reserved for recreational fishing, with no commercial barra fishing allowed. The river runs more than 40km from the Daly River crossing down to Anson Bay, through the Daly–Reynolds floodplains.

Tides of up to seven metres are common and the river can rise and fall by as much as 16m with the seasons, so local knowledge matters. Charters fish the river itself and the coastal creeks of Anson Bay for barramundi, mangrove jack and threadfin salmon.
daly-river.season: The run-off, from about March to May, is the classic time, when big tides draw barra off the floodplains. Note that the lower tidal section of the Daly is closed to fishing from 1 October to 31 January.

p: The Daly is one of the Territory's top barramundi rivers and is reserved for recreational fishing, with no commercial barra fishing. Lined with rainforest and paperbarks, its fallen trees make classic barra snags. The river runs more than 40 km from the Daly River crossing to Anson Bay, through the Daly–Reynolds floodplain system, which has the largest catchment of any major freshwater floodplain in the NT.

Snags, sandbars, S-bends and rock bars; day charters pick up from the local tourist parks
Anson Bay coastal creeks
Saltwater barra, mangrove jack and threadfin salmon; a 220 km down-and-back run by boat from the Daly River ramp
Daly River mouth and Reynolds floodplains
Run-off barra country where big tides push fish off the floodplains; Humbug Fishing's most-booked liveaboard area
Peron Islands and Docherty's Creek
Part of Anson Bay's coastal floodplains and tidal flats

p: The run-off, roughly March to May, is the classic window, but only about two tide cycles a month suit it, so the best dates book out early.
items: Barramundi (run-off)
About March to May, when big tides draw barra off the floodplains into the main channels
Barramundi (dry season)
Fishable year-round; NT Fish & 4x4 runs strict 4-hour half days June to September and its Dry Season Escape July to October
Reef and pelagic fish
Liveaboard trips switch to golden snapper, red emperor and Spanish mackerel on the smaller tides
Daly River public boat ramp, Wooliana Road
Launch point for local day charters and the Anson Bay 'Big Day Out'
Daly River tourist parks
NT Fish & 4x4 collects day-charter guests from local parks
Darwin hotel transfers
Liveaboard and package guests are driven from Darwin; NT Fish & 4x4 also quotes a $900 transfer between Darwin and Daly River for day-charter guests

p: The Daly is about 210–223 km south-west of Darwin, roughly 2.5 hours via the Stuart Highway and Daly River Road. The river can rise and fall by up to 16 m with the seasons and tides of up to 7 m are common, so local knowledge matters. Both freshwater and saltwater crocodiles live in the river.

From 1 October to 31 January NT Fisheries closes the lower Daly seasonal closure area: you may not fish there, keep barramundi or have a baited or hooked line. The NT Fisheries page has a map of the boundary, so check it before planning a trip in those months. Wet-season trips can be redirected if cyclones or flooding cut access.

faq: How far is the Daly River from Darwin?
About 210–223 km south-west, roughly a 2.5-hour drive via the Stuart Highway and Daly River Road. It is about 110 km south-west of Adelaide River.
Is the Daly River closed to fishing at any time of year?

Yes. From 1 October to 31 January NT Fisheries closes the lower Daly seasonal closure area: you may not fish, keep barramundi or have a baited or hooked line there. Check the map on the NT Fisheries page for the exact boundary before planning a trip in those months.
Can you fish the Daly River from a mothership?

Yes. Humbug Fishing runs 5–7 day liveaboard trips from Darwin on its 24 m catamaran Starfire, fishing the Daly River mouth, Anson Bay and the Reynolds floodplains from surveyed tenders, with hotel transfers included.
Are there crocodiles in the Daly River?
Yes, a healthy population of both freshwater and saltwater crocodiles. Fish from a boat or well back from the bank, and never swim.
Is there a minimum group size for Daly River charters?

Usually. NT Fish & 4x4 needs at least two clients for its tours and three for the 12-hour Big Day Out to Anson Bay, and its Dry Season Escape takes two to four people. Mothership trips with Humbug Fishing are booked by private groups of up to 12.
Should I book a day charter or a package on the Daly?

A day charter suits anglers already staying at Daly River: NT Fish & 4x4 collects guests from local parks for half and full days. Visitors without a car can book its packages, which include Darwin pick-up, air-conditioned rooms and meals, or a Humbug mothership trip from Darwin that fishes the river mouth and Anson Bay.

dundee.summary: Dundee Beach fishing charters launch from the seawall-protected Dundee Beach ramp, about 90 minutes from Darwin, for Finniss River barramundi, black jewfish and golden snapper on inshore reefs, and mackerel, queenfish and sailfish out to the Peron Islands. Full days with Dundee Beach Fishing Charters cost $550 per person; multi-day packages with accommodation start at about $2,500 per person.
intro: Dundee Beach is about 90 minutes from Darwin by sealed road, with a boat ramp protected by a seawall, a beachfront tavern and a holiday park. Barramundi fishing centres on the Finniss River and nearby coastal creeks, while reef and sportfishing grounds stretch out to the Peron Islands and Bateman Shoals.
Nearby Bynoe Harbour is sheltered enough for smaller boats and is launched from Keswick Point or the south-shore ramps. Several Dundee operators offer multi-day packages with their own accommodation.
dundee.season: Barramundi are caught year-round, with October often described as the sweet spot when the tides suit. Big black jewfish are taken close to shore, and the wider grounds produce queenfish, giant trevally, Spanish mackerel, tuna and sailfish. Bynoe Harbour sits in a 'storm alley', so keep an eye on the weather radar.

p: The Dundee Coast runs from Native Point to the Peron Islands and is known as the best bluewater fishing within easy reach of Darwin. Some very big black jewfish are caught less than 2 km out, barra are taken along the coast and in the rivers, and wider reefs produce coral trout, red emperor, Spanish mackerel and cobia.

p: Dundee Beach is about 90 minutes from Darwin by sealed road, with a beachfront tavern, holiday park and boat ramp. Several operators have their own accommodation for multi-day packages. Boats in 2C survey can fish up to 15 nautical miles offshore, which opens up the wider reefs.

Bynoe Harbour sits in a 'storm alley', so watch the Bureau of Meteorology radar. Saltwater crocodiles are present in the rivers and creeks. Check tides before booking flights, and check the current NT Fisheries rules for bag and size limits.

faq: How far is Dundee Beach from Darwin?
About 90 minutes by sealed road, according to NT tourism; local operators quote 140–165 km. By sea it can be quicker, depending on the weather.
Why do some Dundee charters fish further offshore than others?
It depends on survey class. Anglers Choice and Dundee Beach Fishing Charters run boats in 2C survey, which lets them fish up to 15 nautical miles offshore and reach the wider reefs.
Is Bynoe Harbour safe for small boats?
Much of Bynoe Harbour is considered sheltered water and can be fished from a small tinny, but it sits in a storm alley, so locals keep an eye on the Bureau of Meteorology radar throughout the day.
Can I stay at Dundee Beach on a fishing package?

Yes. Dundee Beach Fishing Charters' retreat sleeps up to 16 with a pool and chef, Anglers Choice has its own beach house, and Barra or Blue sells 3–5 day all-inclusive packages from its five-bedroom house with a pool. River & Reef added 3–4 day Dundee liveaboard trips on its mothership for 2026.
Should I book a barra day or a reef day at Dundee?

Barra days fish the Finniss River and coastal creeks on suitable tides, and dry-season fish average about 65–80 cm. Reef and bluewater days chase black jewfish, golden snapper, red emperor, mackerel and pelagics on inshore reefs and out towards the Peron Islands. Many anglers on multi-day packages mix both.
Can I do a Dundee Beach charter as a day trip from Darwin?

Yes. Most Dundee day charters leave the ramp at about 7–7:30am and return mid-afternoon, so you drive down early (about 90 minutes) or stay overnight. Alure's shared Dundee day meets at Darwin's Dinah Beach ramp at 5:15am, and Yknot runs full and extended Dundee days from the Dundee ramp.

tiwi-islands.summary: Tiwi Islands fishing charters run as day trips from Leaders Creek, about an hour's drive from Darwin, or as fly-in stays at Tiwi Island Retreat at Port Hurd on Bathurst Island. Golden snapper and black jewfish bite year-round, with queenfish, trevally and mackerel in the dry. Alure's shared day costs $575 per person; the Retreat's three-night package is $4,900.
intro: Bathurst and Melville islands lie about 80km north of Darwin and offer remote, lightly fished water. Day charters run from Leaders Creek — the closest ramp to the Tiwis, about an hour from Darwin — past the Vernon Islands and the Adelaide River mouth, while fly-in guests stay at Port Hurd on western Bathurst Island.
The estuaries hold barramundi, threadfin salmon and mangrove jack, while queenfish, giant trevally, golden snapper and black jewfish patrol the rocky headlands.
tiwi-islands.season: Golden snapper and black jewfish are caught year-round, joined by queenfish, trevally and Spanish mackerel in the dry season. Tiwi fishing operators generally close over the wet season (roughly December to March).

p: Bathurst and Melville islands, about 80 km north of Darwin, offer estuary fishing for barramundi, salmon and mangrove jack and bluewater fishing around rocky headlands for queenfish, giant trevally, golden snapper and black jewfish. Day boats run up from Leaders Creek, while fly-in guests fish from Port Hurd on western Bathurst Island.

p: The Tiwi Islands are Aboriginal land and access needs a permit; the Tiwi Land Council manages permits, and guided operators and the Retreat include or arrange what visitors need. The annual football grand final and art sale in March is the only day permits are not required to travel to the islands.
Saltwater crocodiles are common and box jellyfish are present from October to May, so swimming in the sea is off the menu.

faq: How do you get to the Tiwi Islands to go fishing?

Most day trips launch at Leaders Creek, about an hour's drive from Darwin, and run past the Vernon Islands to the Tiwis. Alternatively, fly from Darwin to Port Hurd on a charter flight and stay at Tiwi Island Retreat. NT tourism says travel is by light aircraft or ferry.
When do Tiwi Islands fishing operators close?
Most close during the tropical summer (wet season). Tiwi Island Retreat closes every year from December to March, though it takes bookings year-round.
Can you catch marlin and sailfish off the Tiwi Islands?
Yes. NT tourism names the Bathurst trench north-west of Bathurst Island, Afghan Shoals south of Cape Fourcroy and Shepparton Shoals to the west as marlin and sailfish grounds.
Can you swim at the Tiwi Islands?
Not in the sea. Tiwi Island Retreat warns that saltwater crocodiles are common and box jellyfish are present from October to May; guests use its beachfront pool instead.
Can you stay on the Tiwi Islands on a mothership?

Yes. Offshore Boats moves its air-conditioned mothership to Melville Island from May to December for barra, reef and sportfishing, with Darwin transfers, meals and Starlink included. Tiwi Island Retreat on Bathurst Island is the land-based alternative.
Do I need a permit to fish the Tiwi Islands?

The Tiwi Islands are Aboriginal land, and visitors need a permit from the Tiwi Land Council. Tiwi Island Retreat includes visitor and fishing permits in its packages, and guided day operators arrange what their guests need, so ask when you book.

arnhem-land.summary: Arnhem Land fishing charters run from Nhulunbuy (Gove), where OBJ Adventures' day trips cost $350–$595 per person, or as fly-in and liveaboard trips: Cobourg Fishing Safaris' camp from $5,300 per person, Dhipirri Lodge on the Glyde River and Australian Sportfishing Charters' Gove mothership. Barramundi peak in the March–June run-off; coral trout, golden snapper and Spanish mackerel suit the dry season.
intro: Arnhem Land offers some of the most remote fishing in Australia. Much of the coast can only be visited and fished legally with permits, usually through accredited fishing tour operators, which is why most anglers come on a guided trip, stay at a fly-in lodge or live aboard a mothership.

Options range from Nhulunbuy (Gove), with day charters on the reefs off the Gove Peninsula and Bremer Island and multi-day motherships into Arnhem and Buckingham bays and the Wessel and English Company islands, to fly-in camps and lodges on the Cobourg Peninsula and in East Arnhem. The Cobourg is better known for bluewater species than barra; the rivers of Arnhem and Buckingham bays are barramundi country.
arnhem-land.season: Barramundi fishing peaks in the estuaries during the run-off (around March to June on the Glyde River). Bluewater and reef species — Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, queenfish, longtail tuna, coral trout and golden snapper — are targeted through the dry season. Camping on the Cobourg Peninsula is limited to May to October.

p: Arnhem Land's coast is cut by dozens of remote tidal rivers that visitors can only reach with permits, which is why most anglers fish with an accredited operator: a day charter out of Nhulunbuy (Gove), a fly-in camp or lodge, or a mothership.

p: All of East Arnhem Land is Aboriginal land, and Commonwealth and NT law require a written permit to enter it, including the intertidal waters over it. The Northern Land Council issues recreational fishing permits for specific fishing zones; in November 2026 its website said recreation applications were temporarily unavailable online, with a downloadable application pack instead. Most of the Gove Peninsula coast is covered by the Dhimurru arrangement, visitors need a general permit to be in Nhulunbuy, and operators usually arrange the permits their trips need.

Parts of Arnhem Land are dry areas where it is illegal to bring alcohol, and takeaway alcohol in Nhulunbuy needs a permit, so ask your operator. Crocodiles are present throughout. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for limits.

faq: How do you get to Nhulunbuy (Gove) to go fishing?

Most visitors fly: Airnorth's flight from Darwin to Gove takes about 1 hour 15 minutes (about 1 hour 50 from Cairns). Driving is about 1,044 km from Darwin, and the Central Arnhem Road needs a Northern Land Council transit permit.
Can I bring alcohol on an Arnhem Land fishing trip?

It depends where you go. Dhipirri Lodge is in a dry area where bringing alcohol is illegal, though the lodge has a licensed bar. In Nhulunbuy you need a permit to buy takeaway alcohol, and Cobourg Fishing Safaris lets guests pre-order drinks at bottle-shop prices.
How much luggage can I take on an Arnhem Land fly-in trip?

Light aircraft limit weight. Cobourg Fishing Safaris recommends no more than 15 kg in a soft bag with rod tubes under 2.4 m, and DNA Barra Fishing's island camp expects about 10 kg with rod tubes no longer than 100 cm.
Can I keep my catch on an Arnhem Land fishing trip?

Policies differ. Cobourg Fishing Safaris lets guests keep fish within NT possession limits and will vacuum-seal and freeze them, while Dhipirri Lodge keeps only what its chef needs and does not let guests take fish home.
Can you do a liveaboard fishing trip in Arnhem Land?

Yes. Australian Sportfishing Charters bases its 65ft mothership Iron Lady at Gove Harbour from February to October and runs 4–7 day shared or private trips for up to eight guests, fishing from guided tenders. Catch is mostly released.
Do I need a permit to fish in Arnhem Land?

Usually. Arnhem Land is Aboriginal land, and entering it or its intertidal waters needs a written permit. Visitors need a general permit to be in Nhulunbuy, and the Northern Land Council issues recreational fishing permits for set zones (its online recreation applications were paused in November 2026). Lodges, camps and charters normally arrange their guests' permits, so check your package.

p: The NT side of the Gulf of Carpentaria is big, remote country. Most visiting anglers come on a fly-in package to Groote Eylandt or a mothership trip on the Roper River, while self-drive anglers base themselves at Borroloola or King Ash Bay on the McArthur River.
