p: Groote Eylandt is Aboriginal land managed through the Anindilyakwa Land Council; Groote Eylandt Lodge organises any permits its guests need and may change bookings at short notice for cultural or weather reasons. Elsewhere, check access and permit requirements with the Northern Land Council before you go.
Saltwater crocodiles are present throughout the Gulf rivers and King Ash Bay advises against swimming. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for bag and size limits.

faq: How do you get to Groote Eylandt for fishing?
Fly with Airnorth from Darwin. Groote Eylandt Lodge's 2–5 day fishing packages include return flights, twin-share rooms, all meals, island transfers and any permits needed.
How far is Borroloola from Darwin?
About 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin, near the Queensland border; from Katherine it is about 7 hours via the Carpentaria Highway. Scheduled flights are also available.
Can you catch billfish in the Gulf of Carpentaria?

Yes. NT tourism says the grounds south of Groote Eylandt are known for large numbers of marlin and sailfish, mainly from November to March, and that billfish are found in good numbers close to the Sir Edward Pellew Islands.
Do I need a permit to fish Groote Eylandt?
Permits are needed to access some land on Groote, which is managed through the Anindilyakwa Land Council. If you fish with Groote Eylandt Lodge, the lodge organises the permits for you.

northern-territory.summary: Most Northern Territory fishing charters leave Darwin: harbour and offshore boats from Cullen Bay, Stokes Hill Wharf and Dinah Beach, and barra guides with pre-dawn hotel pick-up. Barramundi peak in the March–May run-off, while golden snapper and black jewfish bite year-round. Shared day trips cost about $225–$750 per person; fly-in lodges and motherships cost thousands.
intro: The Northern Territory is Australia's barramundi capital. Charters out of Darwin and into the Top End's rivers, floodplains and wilderness areas (the Mary, Daly and Alligator rivers, Kakadu, Dundee Beach and the Tiwi Islands) chase barra alongside threadfin salmon, mangrove jack and saratoga, while fly-in lodges and motherships reach the remote coasts of Arnhem Land and the Gulf of Carpentaria.

Offshore and harbour trips target black jewfish, golden snapper, Spanish mackerel, giant trevally, longtail tuna and sailfish. You don't need a recreational fishing licence in the NT, and many operators run private trips, so your group has the boat and the guide to itself.
northern-territory.season: The Top End has three key periods. The run-off after the wet season (roughly March to May) is prime barramundi time as fish move through flooded creeks and floodplains. The dry season (May to September) brings stable weather that suits offshore and reef trips. The build-up (October to December) is hot and humid but can produce big barra on lures.

p: Most NT charter fishing happens in the Top End, within a day's travel of Darwin. Fly-in lodges, mothership trips and island packages reach the remote coasts of Arnhem Land and the Gulf, and Katherine is a self-drive base for the Victoria, Daly and Roper rivers.

p: You don't need a recreational fishing licence or a recreational boat licence in the NT, but bag, size and possession limits apply, and some areas have their own rules, such as the Mary River fish management zone and the seasonal closure on the lower Daly River (1 October to 31 January). Check the current NT Fisheries rules or the free NT Fishing Mate app before keeping fish.

Visiting or fishing Aboriginal land and waters often needs a permit, from the Northern Land Council, the Tiwi Land Council, the Anindilyakwa Land Council (Groote) or Dhimurru (Gove). Kakadu needs a Parks Australia pass, and most other NT parks need an NT Parks Visitor Pass. Guided trips often include these, so ask your operator.
Saltwater crocodiles live in almost all Top End waterways: be Crocwise and never swim.

faq: What is the barra run-off?

The run-off happens at the end of the wet season, roughly February or March to May, when floodwaters drain off the floodplains into the rivers and creeks. Bait is flushed out and barramundi gather at creek mouths and drains to feed, which makes it the best time of year for a fish over a metre.
Do I need a permit to fish in the Northern Territory?

You don't need a recreational fishing licence, but much of the coast is Aboriginal land, and visiting it often needs a permit from the relevant land council. Fishing with a licensed operator is usually the simplest way, as many include or arrange permits.
Are there crocodiles where NT fishing charters go?

Yes. Saltwater crocodiles are found in Darwin Harbour, the Top End rivers and billabongs, and around the islands. Guided boats are a safe way to fish, but never swim, keep back from the water's edge and follow your guide's advice.
Can I fish the Northern Territory without leaving Darwin?

Yes. Half-day harbour trips leave from Stokes Hill Wharf, Cullen Bay and Dinah Beach for barra, golden snapper, jewfish and mud crabs, and offshore days reach reefs 20–50 km out. Barra guides also run day trips with pre-dawn hotel pick-up to Corroboree Billabong, Shady Camp, Bynoe Harbour and Dundee Beach.
Which NT fishing trips need a flight?

The Tiwi Islands lodge, the Cobourg Peninsula camp, Arnhem Land lodges such as Dhipirri, Gove (Nhulunbuy) and Groote Eylandt are reached by air from Darwin. Lodge, camp and island packages usually include the flights, and light aircraft limit luggage, often to 10–15 kg in a soft bag.
Should I book a shared or private NT fishing charter?

Shared seats suit solo anglers and couples: Darwin harbour half days start at about $225 per person, and barra days to Corroboree Billabong or Shady Camp are about $400–$750 per person. A private boat, from about $1,200 for a half day, gives a group of up to four to six anglers the guide and the plan to themselves.
Can families and beginners go fishing in the NT?

Yes. Darwin Harbour half days are the easiest start: Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters sells a family charter for two adults and three children, Equinox crews bait hooks for beginners, and Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge gives first-timers casting tuition at Shady Camp. Multi-day remote trips often set minimum ages, so check when you book.

intro: Cairns is the main gateway to fishing the northern Great Barrier Reef. Shared and private reef boats leave Marlin Marina for coral trout, red emperor, nannygai and Spanish mackerel, and from September to mid-December game boats work the reef edge between Cairns and Lizard Island for giant black marlin.

Closer to town, Trinity Inlet, a State Marine Park with more than 100 km of creeks and channels, holds barramundi, mangrove jack, fingermark and threadfin, and guides trailer boats to the Mulgrave and Russell rivers about 40 km south. On the Atherton Tablelands, Lake Tinaroo is known for metre-plus stocked barramundi, and several Cairns guides collect anglers from their hotels.
cairns.season: Coral trout, red emperor and nannygai are caught year-round, though bottom fishing is less predictable in the wet (January to March), when mackerel and tuna are often more active. Giant black marlin run from early September to mid-December, and juvenile black marlin are caught within an hour of Cairns much of the year. Saltwater barramundi close from 1 November to 31 January.

p: Cairns charters work four very different kinds of water: the Great Barrier Reef offshore, Trinity Inlet on the city's doorstep, the Mulgrave and Russell rivers to the south, and Lake Tinaroo up on the Atherton Tablelands. Shared reef boats usually fish 30–60 m of water within about 50 km of Cairns.
Further out, the reef edge and continental shelf between Cairns and Lizard Island is where giant black marlin gather each spring.

p: Great Barrier Reef trips attract the Environmental Management Charge (reef tax): $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026 and $9 from 1 April 2027. Some operators include it, others add it, and several reef boats now add a fuel levy.

Coral trout, emperors, cods and other coral reef fin fish are closed around the October and November new moons (8–12 October and 6–10 November in 2026), and Spanish mackerel north of 22°S are closed for three weeks from each of those dates. East-coast barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January, and it is illegal to target them even for catch and release. Saltwater crocodiles live in Trinity Inlet and the rivers, so keep well back from the water's edge.

Fuel levies have become common: one Cairns operator adds a temporary 13% levy to bookings made from 14 October 2026, and the large reef boats add a per-person or per-vessel levy to advertised prices. Ask for the all-up price when you book.

faq: How long does it take to reach the Great Barrier Reef from Cairns?
Shared reef boats allow at least 90 minutes each way and usually fish within about 50 km of Cairns. Light-tackle game boats find juvenile black marlin within about an hour's run of the city.
When is giant black marlin season in Cairns?

Peak season runs from early September to mid-December along about 150 nautical miles of reef edge between Cairns and Lizard Island. Most anglers book liveaboard trips of three to seven days, and most fish are tagged and released.
Where can I catch barramundi near Cairns?

Guides fish Trinity Inlet beside the city and the Mulgrave and Russell rivers about 40 km south, and Lake Tinaroo on the Tablelands holds metre-plus stocked barramundi. Saltwater barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January.
Is there a reef tax on Cairns fishing charters?
Yes. The Great Barrier Reef Environmental Management Charge is $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2027, then $9. Check whether your charter price includes it.
Can I fish Lake Tinaroo on a trip from Cairns?

Yes. Several Cairns barramundi guides run full days on Lake Tinaroo, on the Atherton Tablelands, and collect guests from Cairns accommodation. As a stocked impoundment it is fished while saltwater barramundi are closed; check whether a Stocked Impoundment Permit applies before you go.

intro: The Whitsundays combine island scenery with serious reef fishing. Charters leave Coral Sea Marina at Airlie Beach, Hamilton Island Marina and Cape Gloucester Resort north of Airlie, and fish island grounds that are mostly 40–70 m deep, as well as the outer Great Barrier Reef about 40 nautical miles out.

Coral trout, red emperor, nannygai and sweetlip are year-round targets, while Spanish mackerel, sailfish and light-tackle black marlin add a pelagic option. One Airlie Beach operator holds Yellow Zone certification for areas many charters cannot fish, and several Hamilton Island restaurants will cook your catch.
whitsundays.season: Reef fishing runs year-round. Sailfish are around all year but peak from about August to December. Coral reef fin fish and Spanish mackerel are subject to seasonal closures around October and November — check the current Queensland rules or ask your operator.

p: Most fishing grounds around the Whitsunday Islands sit in 40–70 m of water, a 15–45 minute run from Hamilton Island, with shoals and inner reefs close to Airlie Beach. The outer Great Barrier Reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach, so it is usually fished on full-day or extended private trips.

On reef fin fish closure days some boats run private sport or game trips only. Skippers apply Queensland size and bag limits, so undersized fish go back.
Some prices include the reef tax (Environmental Management Charge) and others add it. Most shared trips allow BYO alcohol in cans only, and some boats run a fuel surcharge if fuel costs rise sharply.

faq: Can you fish the outer Great Barrier Reef from Airlie Beach?

Yes, in good weather. The outer reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach, so it is fished on 8-hour private or 10–11 hour extended trips. Half-day and shared trips fish the island grounds and shoals.
How deep is the water around the Whitsunday Islands?
Most fishing grounds around the islands are 40–70 m deep, depending on location.
Can I go fishing in the Whitsundays during the October and November closures?

Bottom fishing for coral reef fin fish is closed 8–12 October and 6–10 November 2026, and Spanish mackerel 8–29 October and 6–27 November. Some Hamilton Island boats run private sport or game trips on those days instead.
When is sailfish season in the Whitsundays?
Sailfish are caught all year but peak from about August to December. Hamilton Island game boats target them on light tackle and tag and release them.
Can I go fishing in the Whitsundays from Bowen?

There are no Bowen-based listings yet, but a small-group operator based at Cape Gloucester Resort, between Airlie Beach and Bowen, can depart from Bowen by arrangement, and can tow its boat to Bowen or Mackay for an extra fee.

intro: Port Douglas sits closer to the outer Great Barrier Reef than most mainland ports: the larger shared boats reach their reef grounds in about an hour, and game boats run to the shelf for black marlin. Charters leave Crystalbrook Superyacht Marina on Wharf Street, Marano's Fuel Wharf and the public jetty on Ashford Avenue.

Inshore options include the Port Douglas estuaries, fringing reefs and the Low Isles, so small sportfishing boats can switch to the rivers for barramundi and mangrove jack when the wind is up. Liveaboards head north to the Ribbon Reefs and Lizard Island.
port-douglas.season: Reef fishing is year-round, apart from coral reef fin fish closures around October and November. Light-tackle juvenile black marlin run from about July to October, and the giant black marlin season between Cairns and Lizard Island is from around September to mid-December.

p: Port Douglas sits close to the reef: the big shared boats reach most of their grounds in about an hour, while small fast boats split their time between fringing reefs, the Low Isles and the estuaries. Liveaboards head north to the Ribbon Reefs and Lizard Island.

Shared reef boats cap fishing numbers (MV Norseman takes 20 anglers) and gut and bag your catch, as filleting on board isn't permitted. Big boats often have a licensed bar and no BYO, while small sportfishing boats usually allow your own drinks.

Reef trips can switch to the estuaries when the wind is up. Bottom-fishing reef tours stop during the coral reef fin fish closures, and Spanish mackerel are closed for three weeks from 8 October and 6 November 2026. Crocodiles live in the local rivers and estuaries.

faq: How far is the reef from Port Douglas?
Most reef grounds are about an hour's run on the larger charter boats, and local operators say Port Douglas gives closer access to the outer reef than Cairns.
Can I keep my fish on a Port Douglas reef trip?
Yes, legal-size fish within bag limits. Shared reef boats such as MV Norseman gut and bag your catch for you to take home, but they cannot fillet on board.
What do Port Douglas fishing charters do in windy weather?
Small-boat reef trips move into the estuaries and rivers, where barramundi, mangrove jack, fingermark and grunter are on offer. Larger boats such as the 18 m Norseman handle rougher seas.
When can you catch black marlin from Port Douglas?
Juvenile black marlin are targeted on light tackle from about July to October, and giant black marlin from September to mid-December between Cairns and Lizard Island, usually on liveaboard trips.
Can I do a fishing liveaboard from Port Douglas?

Yes. Local operators run mothership trips of at least three nights from Port Douglas or Lizard Island for up to five guests, and 40 ft game boat liveaboards of two to five nights to the Ribbon Reefs, including giant black marlin trips from September to December.

intro: Mackay offers an unusual mix: offshore reef fishing among the Cumberland and Sir James Smith island groups and Great Barrier Reef anchorages such as Square, Stevens and Chauvel reefs, plus the Mackay Net Free Zone, fifteen creek systems from Cape Hillsborough to St Helens Bay, for barramundi, mangrove jack and salmon.

Offshore charters launch from Hay Point, about 30 minutes south of town, while fly and lure guides work the Seaforth flats north of Mackay for golden trevally, queenfish and permit. Inland, Kinchant, Teemburra and Eungella dams hold stocked barramundi, saratoga and sooty grunter, and stay open when the saltwater barra season is closed.
mackay.season: Creek barramundi, jacks and salmon fish best from about February to May while the water stays warm. Reef species and Spanish mackerel come on from around June as the weather settles, with August and September good for offshore jigging. During the saltwater barra closure (1 November to 31 January) anglers turn to the dams.

p: Mackay mixes three fisheries: creeks and flats in the Mackay Net Free Zone, offshore islands and the Great Barrier Reef, and stocked barramundi dams in the Pioneer Valley hinterland.

Barramundi in tidal waters are closed from 1 November to 31 January, but the stocked dams stay open. Mackay is north of 22°S, so the northern Spanish mackerel closures apply: 8–29 October and 6–27 November in 2026. Estuarine crocodiles occur in Mackay's creeks and rivers.

faq: What is the Mackay Net Free Zone?

A net-free stretch of coast from Cape Hillsborough to the northern end of St Helens Bay, covering fifteen creek systems plus inlets, beaches and mangrove flats. It holds barramundi, grunter, mangrove jack and salmon, with all-tide ramps at Victor Creek, Seaforth and Murray Creek.
Can you catch barramundi in Mackay during the closed season?
Yes, in the stocked dams. Teemburra, Kinchant and Eungella dams stay open while saltwater barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January; the afternoon, dusk and night bites are best.
Where do Mackay reef charters fish?

Around island groups in 30–40 m of water (Sir James Smith, Cumberland and Beverley), out past Scawfell Island where red fish appear at about 50 m, and at Great Barrier Reef anchorages such as Square, Stevens and Chauvel reefs.
Is there fly fishing in Mackay?
Yes. A local guide runs fly and lure trips on the Seaforth flats for golden trevally, queenfish, permit and blackspot tuskfish, and on Kinchant and Teemburra dams for barramundi.
Do I need a permit to fish Mackay's barramundi dams?

Kinchant, Teemburra and Eungella are stocked dams, and Queensland requires a Stocked Impoundment Permit for dams in its permit scheme. Check the current list on the Queensland Government website before you go, or ask your guide.

intro: Townsville is a gateway to the central Great Barrier Reef. From Breakwater Marina, larger charter boats reach the first reef drop in about 1.5–2 hours, so reef trips are long: 13-hour days, 12-hour nights and extended 16–23 hour trips for red emperor, nannygai, coral trout and red-throat emperor.

Across Cleveland Bay, Magnetic Island has 23 bays and beaches, 14 of them fishable, with wrecks, shoals and mangroves, and private charters from Horseshoe Bay also run up to 50 nautical miles offshore. The Hinchinbrook Channel barramundi grounds are about 1.5 hours' drive north.
townsville.season: Reef species are targeted year-round, weather permitting, on both day and night trips. Spotted mackerel and tuna are trolled around Magnetic Island's bays. Coral reef fin fish closures apply around October and November.

p: Townsville reef trips are long because the first reef drop is 1.5–2 hours away on a fast boat, so day trips run about 13 hours and many go overnight. Magnetic Island charters fish the island's bays and wrecks or run out to offshore shoals.

Magnetic Island charters are private only, with up to five guests inshore and four offshore, and guests can bring their own food and drinks. Townsville waters are within crocodile habitat, so take care around estuaries.

faq: How long does it take to reach the reef from Townsville?
About 1.5–2 hours from Breakwater Marina to the first reef drop on a fast charter boat, depending on the weather. That is why most Townsville reef trips run 12–13 hours or longer.
Can I join a Townsville reef trip on my own?
Yes. Mixed-group charters sell individual spots on 12–13 hour reef trips with up to 12 people. They are opened when the weather suits and need to fill before they go.
Can you fish around Magnetic Island?

Yes. Of the island's 23 bays and beaches, 14 are fishable, with wrecks, shoals, fringing reef and mangroves. Charters from Horseshoe Bay troll for spotted mackerel and tuna and bottom fish for coral trout and tuskfish.
Can I do an overnight reef fishing trip from Townsville?
Yes. Full-boat night trips of about 12 hours leave Breakwater Marina at 3 pm, and extended 16–23 hour trips fish through the night. Multi-day trips also run from Lucinda and Camp Island Lodge.

intro: The Daintree River is the region's largest river, with more than 25 km of navigable water lined by mangroves and World Heritage rainforest. Fishing trips leave from the public wharf and boat ramp beside the Daintree River ferry crossing on Cape Tribulation Road, Lower Daintree.

Barramundi are the main target, caught on lure and fly outside the closed season, alongside mangrove jack, fingermark and mud crabs. On calm days guides add Snapper Island, wrecks and inshore reefs off the river mouth, and with plenty of saltwater crocodiles and birdlife, many trips double as nature tours.
daintree.season: Barramundi bite every month, with the best fishing from about September to March — but the east-coast barramundi closed season runs from 1 November to 31 January, when guides switch to other species.

p: The Daintree River is the region's largest river, with more than 25 km of navigable water through mangroves, farmland and World Heritage rainforest. On calm days guides also run out to the islands, wrecks and inshore reefs off the river mouth.

p: The river is home to plenty of saltwater crocodiles and rich birdlife, so many fishing trips double as nature tours. Keep away from the water's edge, keep hands inside the boat and bin fish scraps.

Barramundi are closed on Queensland's east coast from 1 November to 31 January, and deliberately targeting them, even for catch and release, is prohibited. River trips use small boats for two to three anglers or a shaded catamaran for families, and most supply bait and tackle; bring your own food and drinks on the share trips.

faq: Are there crocodiles in the Daintree River?
Yes. The river has plenty of saltwater crocodiles and spotting them is part of many fishing trips. Follow your guide's instructions, stay back from the water's edge and keep limbs inside the boat.
Can you fish the Daintree for barramundi in November?

No. The east-coast barramundi closed season runs from 1 November to 31 January, and deliberately targeting barra, even catch and release, is prohibited then. Guides switch to mangrove jack and other species.
Can Daintree fishing trips go out to the reef?
On calm days, yes. Guides can add Snapper Island, nearby wrecks and inshore reefs at the river mouth for coral trout and Spanish mackerel, usually on three-quarter or full-day trips.
Can I be picked up from Port Douglas for a Daintree fishing trip?

Some barramundi guides based in Cairns collect guests from Cairns and Port Douglas accommodation and fish the Daintree as one of their rivers. Local Daintree guides usually meet you at the ferry crossing wharf or ramp.

intro: Weipa sits on Albatross Bay on the Gulf side of Cape York, about an hour's flight from Cairns, which makes it one of the more accessible remote fishing towns in Australia. South-easterly winds blow offshore for around nine months of the year, keeping the Gulf side fishable when the east coast is rough.

Guides fish the rivers and estuaries around Albatross Bay for barramundi, threadfin and jacks, and the flats, beaches and headlands for permit, golden trevally, queenfish and tuna. Most visitors book multi-day packages with accommodation, meals and transfers, and later in the season mothership trips reach remote rivers, the Torres Strait and the east-coast reef flats.
weipa.season: Weipa guides work from about late March to mid December and stop for the wet season. Barramundi are most active just after the wet in April and May, longtail tuna are most prolific from April to July, and Spanish mackerel are around all year. Lodge packages run roughly April to November; mothership trips run July to December.

p: Weipa sits on Albatross Bay on the Gulf side of Cape York, with rivers, flats, beaches, headlands and offshore grounds all within easy reach of town. Some guiding is done on foot along remote beaches and rocks.

p: Most visitors book five-to-seven-day all-inclusive packages with transfers, meals and accommodation, and fishing is largely catch and release. Mobile coverage reaches only about 10 km from town, so expect to be out of range on the water.
Weipa waters hold crocodiles, box jellyfish, stonefish, sharks and stingrays, so wade only where your guide says it's safe. Gulf barramundi have a closed season starting on 7 October.
The long-running Fish's Fly & Sportfishing business now trades as Flux Fly Fishing under owner Kurt Rowlands, and still runs both fly and conventional sportfishing trips.

faq: How do you get to Weipa for a fishing trip?

Fly from Cairns: QantasLink flies to Weipa twice daily on most days, a flight of about an hour. Luggage is limited to one 23 kg item, so tape rod tubes to your bag. Guides usually include airport transfers.
Can you fly fish in Weipa?

Yes. Weipa is a well-known saltwater fly destination, with permit, blue bastards, golden trevally and queenfish on the flats, barramundi and threadfin in the estuaries, and pelagics on offshore bait balls. One local operation now runs fly-only trips.
Is fishing in Weipa catch and release?
Mostly. Local guides run largely catch-and-release operations, but you can usually eat fish during your stay, and some allow a small package to take home.
Is there phone reception when fishing out of Weipa?
Coverage reaches only about 10 km from the town centre, so expect to be out of range on the water. Guide boats carry VHF radios, and long-range trips carry a satellite phone.
Are there mothership fishing trips from Weipa?

Yes. One Weipa operator runs mothership charters on a 65 ft vessel that start and end in Weipa, for at least four days and up to six guests. Another runs 5–6 day trips aboard a 27 m mothership joined at Horn Island, on the western rivers and Torres Strait from July to September and the east-coast reef flats from October to December.

intro: Karumba, at the mouth of the Norman River on the Gulf of Carpentaria, is a classic Gulf fishing town. Estuary trips fish the sheltered Norman River and nearby creeks such as Bynoe, Broncos and Brannigans for barramundi, king and blue threadfin, black jewfish and grunter.

Offshore trips run 40–50 km into the Gulf for Spanish mackerel, cobia, fingermark and queenfish when the weather allows, and remote camping charters reach lightly fished rivers around Karumba and Normanton. Some Cairns-based guides also run multi-day Karumba barramundi packages.
karumba.season: Dedicated barramundi trips run from about February to April and again in September and early October; barramundi can't be targeted during the Gulf closed season, which starts on 7 October. Offshore species are fished year-round, weather permitting.

p: Karumba is remote, so most visiting anglers either fly into Normanton and transfer by road or drive across from the east coast. Local charters supply gear and bait, and many allow BYO alcohol in cans.

Barramundi can't be targeted during the Gulf closed season, which starts on 7 October. One local charter keeps catch on ice but, citing Queensland rules, does not fillet on board. The Gulf is crocodile country, so stay back from the water's edge.

Gulf rules differ from the east coast: the Gulf Spanish mackerel limit is 3 per person or 6 per boat, with a higher limit on licensed charter trips of 48 hours or more entirely in Gulf waters. Check the current Queensland rules before you go.

faq: When can you fish for barramundi in Karumba?

Dedicated barramundi charters run from February to April and again from September until 7 October, when the Gulf closed season starts. Outside those windows charters target threadfin, jewfish, mackerel and other species.
How far offshore do Karumba fishing charters go?
Offshore trips run about 40–50 km into the Gulf of Carpentaria for Spanish mackerel, cobia, fingermark, trevally and queenfish, weather permitting.
How do I get to Karumba for a fishing trip?
Fly into Normanton and transfer to Karumba by road; some multi-day packages include the transfer. Many anglers also drive across from the east coast.
Can I book a Karumba fishing package from Cairns?

Yes. A Cairns-based lure and fly guide sells four-day Karumba barramundi packages with five nights' accommodation and meals for up to five anglers, including Normanton–Karumba transfers but not flights. Local Karumba operators also take direct bookings.

intro: The Hinchinbrook Channel, a protected mangrove-lined passage between Hinchinbrook Island and the mainland, is one of north Queensland's best-known barramundi fisheries. Guides launch from the Dungeness ramp at Lucinda, about 15 minutes from Ingham, or from Cardwell for Missionary Bay at the island's northern end.

Besides barramundi, the channel's creeks, flats, rock bars and drains hold mangrove jack, fingermark, threadfin salmon, trevally, queenfish and grunter, and the 5 km Lucinda sugar-loading jetty is a giant fish-attracting structure. In good weather larger boats run out to the islands and the Great Barrier Reef. Lucinda is about 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville.
hinchinbrook.season: Barramundi are the headline species outside the east-coast closed season (1 November to 31 January). Mangrove jack, fingermark, threadfin salmon, trevally and queenfish can be fished year-round, including during the barra closure. Estuarine crocodiles live in the channel, so keep well back from the water's edge.

p: Launch at Dungeness from half tide up: near low tide the end of the ramp can be almost exposed, and on big tides the channel bar can't be crossed for about two hours either side of low. Lucinda is about 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville and 2.5 hours south of Cairns.

The channel is within the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park and World Heritage Area, so check zoning maps; green zones are no-take. Estuarine crocodiles live in the channel and creeks: keep back from the bank, don't wade in for snagged lures and bin your fish frames.

faq: Can I fish for barramundi year-round in the Hinchinbrook Channel?
No. Barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January. Mangrove jack, fingermark, threadfin salmon and other species stay open, so guides keep fishing through the closure.
When is the best tide to launch at the Dungeness ramp in Lucinda?
Half tide to high tide. Near low tide the end of the ramp can be almost exposed, and on big tides the channel bar can be impassable for about two hours either side of low.
Where is Missionary Bay?
At the northern end of Hinchinbrook Island. It is a large protected waterway with nine creeks, deep holes and rock bars, and charters reach it by launching from Cardwell.
How far is the Hinchinbrook Channel from Townsville?
About 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville to Lucinda, and about 2.5 hours south of Cairns. Some guides include Townsville Airport transfers with multi-day packages.
Can I fish offshore from Lucinda?

Yes, in good weather. Offshore guides run to island and reef grounds, including the Great Barrier Reef, for coral trout, Spanish mackerel and nannygai, and GT popping can start right at the end of the Lucinda sugar loader.

Calm-water charters stay inside on the Broadwater and the rivers.

Catch handling varies by boat: some crews clean and bag your fish, but Fish The Deep doesn't clean fish and legally can't fillet, so bring an esky and leave it in the car. Shared offshore trips run five to five and a half hours, with early-morning and late-morning or afternoon departures; seven- and nine-hour days head wider. faq: How far offshore do Gold Coast fishing charters go?

Half-day trips typically fish reefs about 10-20 km out in 33-50 m of water, 15-30 minutes from the Seaway. Full days run 10-35 km offshore into 50-95 m, although strong December-January currents can force boats back onto the closer grounds.
Are there calm-water fishing trips on the Gold Coast?

Yes. Small-boat charters fish the Broadwater, Nerang River and Jumpinpin for flathead, whiting, bream and mangrove jack, a good option for kids or rough days. BKs runs private calm-water trips for up to three people from Runaway Bay or Paradise Point.
Can you see whales on a Gold Coast fishing charter?

Yes, in season. Humpback whales migrate past the Gold Coast from June to October, and operators such as BKs and True Blue mention whales during fishing trips. BKs and Hooker 1 also run dedicated whale-watching tours.
What is the minimum age on Gold Coast fishing charters?
It depends on the boat. BKs takes children from six, while True Blue and Fish The Deep set a minimum age of seven on shared trips; True Blue takes younger children on private bookings.
Do Gold Coast fishing charters clean your fish?
It depends on the boat. BKs bleeds, guts and ices the catch, while Fish The Deep doesn't clean fish. Bring an esky and leave it in the car either way.

Snapper, pearl perch, teraglin, cobia and mackerel are the staples, with mahi mahi, wahoo, tuna and marlin in the warmer months.
Inside the Seaway, the Broadwater, Nerang River and Jumpinpin offer calm-water trips for flathead, bream, whiting and mangrove jack, a good choice for families or when the bar is rough.

faq: How long does it take to reach the offshore grounds from Brisbane?

From Manly, boats cross Moreton Bay and exit through the South Passage bar. Frenzy Charters puts the run at about 1 hour 15 minutes, or around 2.5 hours for continental-shelf trips, which is why most Brisbane offshore charters are full days only.
Can a Brisbane charter pick me up from North Stradbroke Island?

Yes. Frenzy Charters and Moreton Island Fishing Charters both offer pick-ups from Amity Point by arrangement. Moreton Island Fishing Charters can also collect from the Bay Islands, and from Moreton Island on private charters.
Are there calm-water fishing trips near Brisbane for kids?

Yes. Fish Moreton runs two- and four-hour smooth-water trips in the Pumicestone Passage behind Bribie Island for flathead, bream, whiting and tailor, and Brisbane Fishing Tour guides private lure-fishing trips for one to four people on Moreton Bay and the Brisbane River.
Why do Brisbane charters switch to trolling in summer?

A strong East Australian Current combined with northerly winds can make it hard to fish the bottom, so operators such as Frenzy Charters switch to trolling for mahi mahi, wahoo, mackerel, marlin and tuna, including around the FADs.
Is there a snapper closure in Moreton Bay?

Yes. Snapper and pearl perch are closed to take in all Queensland tidal waters, including Moreton Bay and offshore Brisbane, from 15 July to 15 August each year. Charters still run, targeting other reef species.
intro: Brisbane's fishing charters centre on Moreton Bay. Offshore boats leave Manly Boat Harbour or Sandstone Point near Bribie Island, cross the bay and exit through the South Passage bar to grounds such as the Point Lookout reefs, Cape Moreton, Flinders Reef and Hutchinsons Shoals. The run takes about 1 hour 15 minutes, or up to 2.5 hours to the shelf, so most offshore trips are full days.

Inside the bay, small private guides lure-fish Moreton Bay and the Brisbane River for snapper, flathead, jewfish and threadfin, and the calm Pumicestone Passage behind Bribie Island suits families chasing flathead, bream, whiting and tailor.
brisbane.season: Snapper, pearl perch, amberjack, kingfish and teraglin are the main offshore targets in the cooler months. In summer, charters often switch to trolling for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna, wahoo and mackerel. Snapper and pearl perch have a closed season from 15 July to 15 August.

faq: How far are the reefs from Noosa?

Sunshine Reef and North Reef, the half-day grounds, are about 30-45 minutes from Noosa (Deep Sea Fishing Co. quotes 20-40 minutes). Seven- and nine-hour trips run about 1.5-2 hours each way to Chardons Reef, Double Island, the Banks and the Hards.
Which Sunshine Coast charters reach the Barwon Banks?

Salty's nine-hour trip from Caloundra heads 40 km+ to the Barwon Banks, about 1-1.5 hours each way, and its 12-hour trip can reach the Hards. From Noosa, Noosa Bluewater's nine-hour trip runs out to Double Island, the Banks and the Hards.
Are there calm-water fishing trips on the Sunshine Coast?
Yes. Salty's Fishing Charters runs four-hour family trips in the northern Pumicestone Passage from Pelican Waters Marina for bream, flathead and whiting, with child and pensioner prices.
Is dawn the best time for snapper off Noosa?

Usually. Noosa Bluewater Charters says low light combined with a tide change often triggers a feeding spell that doesn't last all day, so dawn tends to beat mid-morning, and late autumn through winter is the best season.
Is Mooloolaba, Noosa or Caloundra better for a fishing charter?

All three fish the same broad reef system. Noosa boats reach their half-day reefs fastest, Caloundra is closest to the Barwon Banks, and Mooloolaba sits in between, with five- to 12-hour trips on a 16-passenger catamaran. Choose by departure point and trip length.

Not usually. Both local operators, Keely Rose and Rainbow Beach Fishing Charters, run full days only, leaving between about 5 and 5:30am and returning mid-afternoon.
Why do I need to call the day before a Rainbow Beach charter?

Departure times shift with daylight and sea conditions. Keely Rose asks every passenger to phone the day before to confirm the time and that conditions are suitable, and to check the trip is definitely going ahead before travelling to Rainbow Beach.
Where should I stay for an early charter at Rainbow Beach?

Can I pay by card on a Rainbow Beach charter boat?

Boats leave around first light, about 5-5:30am, and return mid-afternoon, and operators confirm sea conditions the day before. rainbow-beach.season: Reef fishing runs through the year, weather permitting, with snapper and pearl perch the headline species. Snapper and pearl perch have a Queensland closed season from 15 July to 15 August.

Hervey Bay's charters are small private boats priced per person on a sliding scale, so the more anglers, the less each pays. Published prices run from about $300-$750 per person for a half day and $450-$950 for a full day, depending on whether one, two or three anglers share the boat, with the Breaksea Spit topwater trip at $1,000-$2,000 per person. Hervey Bay Fly and Sportfishing adds a 5-10% fuel surcharge, and both operators take a deposit to hold dates.

faq: Why is Hervey Bay good for fishing when it's windy?

K'gari (Fraser Island) shelters the bay from the prevailing south-easterly trade winds, and the creeks of the Great Sandy Strait give extra options, so guides can usually find fishable water. Hervey Bay Fly and Sportfishing offers all-weather options for this reason.
Can you fly fish in Hervey Bay?

Yes. Hervey Bay's flats are regarded as one of the birthplaces of Australian flats fishing, with golden trevally, longtail tuna and juvenile black marlin cruising the shallows. Hervey Bay Fly and Sportfishing supplies Sage fly outfits.
Can a Hervey Bay charter pick me up from K'gari?
Yes. Hervey Bay Fly and Sportfishing (for an extra $50) and Saltwater Playground Co. (for a small fee) can both collect guests from Kingfisher Bay Resort on K'gari.
How far is Breaksea Spit from Hervey Bay?
It's a long run: Saltwater Playground Co.'s Breaksea topwater trip allows about four hours of travel (two each way) within a 4am-4pm day, targeting giant trevally and Spanish mackerel.
hervey-bay.season: Snapper move into the bay from late autumn and peak in mid-winter (snapper and pearl perch are closed to take from 15 July to 15 August). Longtail tuna are a mainstay from about February to May, golden trevally, queenfish and Spanish mackerel fire in late winter and spring, and summer brings surface schools with juvenile black marlin and mackerel.
intro: Hervey Bay is sheltered from the south-east trade winds by K'gari (Fraser Island), so guides can usually find fishable water. It's also where northern and southern species overlap: snapper and whiting alongside threadfin, queenfish, golden trevally and even barramundi.

Charters leave Urangan Boat Harbour and the Jetty Street ramp for the bay's artificial reefs, ledges such as Moon Ledge, Platypus Bay and the western side of K'gari, while the flats offer sight fishing for golden trevally and longtail tuna on fly or spin. Specialist trips make the long run to Breaksea Spit for giant trevally.

p: Unlike the Town of 1770 to the north, Bundaberg has a maintained deep-water port with no designated bar crossing and no tidal restrictions, so departure times aren't set by the tide. Reef charters here are small: Truansea takes up to six anglers and the river charters two to four.
If you want to keep fish, leave an esky with ice in the car. Burnett Heads is about four and a half hours' drive from Brisbane, or under an hour's flight to Bundaberg.

Published 2026 prices: Truansea's five-hour inshore reef trip is $250 per person and its ten-hour wide trip $400, or $2,400 for a private boat of up to six. Burnett River trips cost $700 for up to four (five hours) with Truansea, or $150 per adult for four hours and $300 for eight with Bundaberg River Fishing Charters, with child rates.

faq: Is there a bar crossing at Bundaberg?
No. Bundaberg has a maintained deep-water port at Burnett Heads with no designated bar crossing and no tidal restrictions, unlike the Town of 1770 to the north, so trips aren't timed around the tide.
How long is the run to the reef from Bundaberg?

Half-day trips fish inshore reefs from a few miles out to about 20 nautical miles. Full days often go wide toward the shelf, around 50 nautical miles away, with two or more hours of travel each way at speed.
What can I do in Bundaberg if it's too windy to go offshore?

Fish the Burnett River. Truansea Charters and Bundaberg River Fishing Charters both run calm-water river and estuary trips for bream, whiting, flathead, mangrove jack and blue salmon that stay in sheltered water when the wind is up.
How far is Bundaberg from Brisbane?
About four and a half hours' drive, or less than an hour's flight, according to local operator Truansea Charters.
intro: Bundaberg's fishing charters leave Burnett Heads, a deep-water port with no bar crossing and no tidal restrictions, so getting offshore is straightforward. Reef grounds run from a few miles out to about 50 nautical miles at the shelf, and full-day trips often travel two hours or more each way to reach coral trout and red emperor country.

The fishing mixes southern species such as big snapper with northern ones such as Spanish mackerel and coral trout, and the Burnett River offers calm-water trips for bream, whiting, flathead, mangrove jack and grunter when the wind is up.
bundaberg.season: Reef fishing runs year-round, weather permitting. p: Most Gladstone liveaboards are self-guided and ask you to bring your own fishing gear; starter bait and ice are often supplied, and the catch is processed and frozen for you to take home. On boats that fish from self-drive dories, you'll need a recreational boat licence.

The Capricorn Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones: Heron Island is largely green zone and so is part of Wistari Reef, so skippers fish the open zones. Gladstone is about an hour's flight from Brisbane, with the airport roughly 10 minutes by taxi from the marina, or about six hours' drive.

Eastern Voyager publishes per-person prices for its Swain Reefs trips: $3,900 for six nights and $4,350 for seven, based on groups of 15-20, with a $750 deposit once numbers are reached. Other Gladstone liveaboards quote whole-boat rates on request, so contact them with your group size and preferred dates.

faq: Are there day fishing trips from Gladstone?

Very few. Gladstone's reef charters are almost all multi-day liveaboards to the Capricorn Bunker Group, the Swains and the Coral Sea. For a single day on the reef, the nearest listed day charters leave from Burnett Heads (Bundaberg), the Town of 1770 and Rosslyn Bay near Yeppoon.
How long are Gladstone reef fishing trips?

Night Crossing runs Friday-to-Thursday Swains trips, MV Mikat runs a minimum of three days to the Capricorn Bunker Group and seven to ten days to the Swains, and Eastern Voyager runs four to ten-plus nights. Coral Sea trips need about ten days.
Do I need a boat licence on a Gladstone liveaboard?

Often, yes. To drive one of Night Crossing's fishing dories you need a recreational ship master (boat) licence from any Australian state or territory, and Eastern Voyager's packing list includes a copy of your boat licence.
Can individuals join a Gladstone fishing liveaboard?

On some boats. Eastern Voyager runs organised Swains trips that individuals and small groups can join (at least 15 people are needed to run) and keeps a waiting list for spare places on group bookings.
Can I snorkel or dive on a Gladstone fishing liveaboard?
Not on all of them. Night Crossing is fishing-only, with no scuba, spearfishing or snorkelling, while MV Mikat suggests bringing snorkelling gear.
intro: Gladstone is the jumping-off point for multi-day reef fishing trips on the southern Great Barrier Reef. Liveaboards leave Gladstone Marina for the Capricorn and Bunker Group about 50 nautical miles offshore, the remote Swain Reefs about 120 nautical miles out, and on longer trips the Coral Sea reefs up to 260 nautical miles away.

Trips typically run four to ten-plus nights, fishing for coral trout, red throat emperor and red emperor, with Spanish mackerel trolled off the reef edges. Most boats fish from dories or tenders so small groups can spread out across the reef, and catches are cleaned and frozen on board to take home.

Check Great Barrier Reef Marine Park zoning: most of Heron Island and part of Wistari Reef are green zones.

p: Commercial netting no longer operates in the Yeppoon area, and locals credit this with better fishing. The coast is inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park: around Byfield, Farnborough Beach and most of Nine Mile Beach are yellow (conservation park) zones, while Corio Bay is mostly general use. Free zoning maps are available from GBRMPA, QPWS and tackle shops.

Rosslyn Bay is sheltered behind a large volcanic headland, and its Fisherman's Co-op sells local reef fish, prawns, bugs and mud crabs. On liveaboards that use tender dinghies, you'll need a boat licence to drive one.

Double Threat Charters publishes 2026 prices for its nine-plus-hour day trips: $500 per person on a mixed-group Wreck & Fern day or $600 on Reef & Shoals, or $5,000 and $6,000 for the whole boat. Extended 18-36-hour trips and Kanimbla's seven- and ten-day liveaboards are priced on enquiry.

faq: How far is Yeppoon from Rockhampton?
Yeppoon is about 45 km north-east of Rockhampton on the Scenic Highway, and Rosslyn Bay Harbour, where the charters leave, is about seven minutes' drive south of Yeppoon.
Can I fish the Swain Reefs from Yeppoon?

Yes. Kanimbla Charters runs seven-day Swains liveaboards from Rosslyn Bay, leaving Friday evening and returning about 5am the next Friday, and Double Threat Charters' 18-36-hour extended trips can reach the Swains in suitable weather.
Is there netting on the Capricorn Coast?

No longer. Commercial netting isn't operational around Yeppoon, and the local tourism site says many anglers believe it has improved the fishing, including for barramundi and fingermark in estuaries such as Corio Bay.
Are there green zones near Yeppoon?

The coast is in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park. Around Byfield, Farnborough Beach and most of Nine Mile Beach are yellow (conservation park) zones with fishing limits, while Corio Bay is mostly general use. Check a current zoning map from GBRMPA, QPWS or a tackle shop.
intro: Yeppoon fishing charters leave Rosslyn Bay Marina, about seven minutes south of town, to fish the deeper reefs, wrecks and shoals of Keppel Bay for red emperor, goldband snapper, large-mouth nannygai and coral trout. The Capricorn Coast is also a base for week-long liveaboard trips to the Swains and the Coral Sea, which suit experienced groups wanting days of reef fishing far offshore. Commercial netting no longer operates around Yeppoon, which locals credit with better inshore fishing.

p: Queensland uses possession limits, not daily bag limits: the limit is the total you can hold at any time, including fish already in your freezer, and unlisted tidal species have a general limit of 20. Closed seasons protect species while they spawn, and you shouldn't target those fish during a closure.

Queensland has no general recreational fishing licence for tidal waters, but a Stocked Impoundment Permit is needed to fish some dams. Coral reef fin fish closures fall around the new moons in October and November each year (8-12 October and 6-10 November in 2026); check the current DAF closed-seasons page or the Qld Fishing 2.0 app for later years.

p: Much of the coast north of Bundaberg lies in the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, and the Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones. You can't fish in a green zone, but you can travel through with fish on board if your gear is stowed. Further south, Moreton Bay is a zoned marine park (Scarborough Reef is a yellow zone and Scotts Point a green zone), and Hervey Bay and the Great Sandy Strait sit in the Great Sandy Marine Park, whose zoning Noosa operators also point anglers to. Check the current map before fishing; free maps are available from GBRMPA, QPWS and tackle shops.

faq: Is a Queensland possession limit the same as a daily bag limit?

No. A possession limit is the total number of a species you can hold at any one time, including fish already at home in the freezer, so it isn't reset each day. Species not listed for tidal waters have a general possession limit of 20.
Can I fillet reef fish on a boat in Queensland?

Yes, with conditions: coral reef fin fish can be carried whole, gilled, gutted or filleted, but fillets must be at least 40 cm long with skin and scales on, and blue-spotted coral trout can't be filleted on board. Some charters don't fillet at all.
When are Queensland's reef fish closures?

Coral reef fin fish such as coral trout and red emperor have two five-day closed seasons in October and November (8-12 October and 6-10 November in 2026), from Cape York south to latitude 24 50' S. Snapper and pearl perch are closed statewide from 15 July to 15 August.
Which part of Queensland is best for a reef fishing charter?

It depends on the trip. The Great Barrier Reef begins off Agnes Water and 1770, and Gladstone and Yeppoon run multi-day liveaboards to the Swain Reefs. Further north, Cairns and Port Douglas boats reach the outer reef in about an hour or two, while southern charters fish subtropical reefs for snapper and pearl perch.
When is barramundi season in Queensland?

On the east coast, barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January to protect spawning fish, and the Gulf of Carpentaria has its own closure. Outside those dates barramundi are open, and some stocked dams can be fished year-round with a Stocked Impoundment Permit.
intro: Queensland stretches from the subtropical Gold Coast to the tip of Cape York, and the fishing changes as you head north. Southern charters target snapper, pearl perch and seasonal pelagics such as mahi mahi, Spanish mackerel and marlin. From Agnes Water and 1770 northwards, the Great Barrier Reef brings coral trout, red emperor, nannygai and giant trevally, while rivers and estuaries hold barramundi, mangrove jack and threadfin salmon.

Hooked Trips lists charters across South East Queensland (Gold Coast, Brisbane and Moreton Bay, Sunshine Coast), the Fraser Coast and Bundaberg, the southern Great Barrier Reef (Agnes Water, Gladstone, Yeppoon), and north through Mackay, the Whitsundays, Townsville, Hinchinbrook, Cairns, Port Douglas, the Daintree, Weipa and Karumba.
queensland.season: Reef fishing runs year-round, with calmer seas more common from late winter through spring. Cairns is famous for giant black marlin from about September to December. Reef fishing for red emperor and coral trout is available all year, weather permitting.

p: Ningaloo Marine Park is zoned, including sanctuary zones, and licensed charters work within the zoning; check it before fishing your own boat. Paying guests on a licensed fishing tour don't need their own Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence, and some operators include a WA fishing licence anyway. Marlin are usually tagged and released, while reef fish are filleted and bagged for you. Gascoyne demersal bag and size limits changed from 1 June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules. Lunch is included on some boats and BYO on others.

faq: Can you catch marlin from a day charter in Exmouth?

Yes. The continental shelf runs close to the coast, so full-day charters from Tantabiddi and Exmouth Marina target blue, black and striped marlin and sailfish. Private gameboat days typically run about eight to nine hours, and marlin are usually tagged and released.
When is sailfish season in Exmouth Gulf?

Operators sell dedicated Exmouth Gulf sailfish days only in October and November, when large numbers of sailfish follow bait schools into the sheltered gulf. It is a light-tackle, sight-casting style of fishing.
Can I join a shared fishing charter in Exmouth?

Yes. Shared full-day bottom-fishing trips with accommodation pickup run from Exmouth Marina. One gameboat also matches anglers for shared offshore days with a minimum of four and a maximum of six, and some reef boats sell single seats to solo anglers.
Can you do a fishing live-aboard from Exmouth?

Yes. Exmouth operators run two- to five-day Ningaloo trips, three- to five-day island trips as far as Thevenard and Barrow islands, four-day remote island packages with island accommodation, and four- to six-day Montebello Islands trips.

Tides set creek trip times all year.

p: The reef boat moors offshore, and guests are taken out by tender from Gantheaume Beach or Entrance Point after a free bus pickup at about 7am. Creek boats launch from Roebuck Bay landings or Entrance Point boat ramp. Most Broome operators include accommodation pickup.

Broome's tidal range can exceed nine metres, so trip times shift daily and wading the flats on a rising tide is dangerous. Saltwater crocodiles live in the creeks and mangroves. Demersal fishing remains open in the North West, but North Coast bag and size limits changed from 1 June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules. Licensed charter clients don't need a boat fishing licence.

faq: Should I book a creek trip or a reef trip in Broome?

Creek trips use small boats for barramundi, threadfin and mangrove jack, usually for up to three or four anglers, and are timed to the tide. Reef trips go 10 to 40 nautical miles offshore on a larger boat for red emperor, coral trout and mackerel, and suit families and groups.
How big are Broome's tides?
Broome's tidal range can exceed nine metres, which is why charters plan creek trips around the tide and departure times change from day to day.
Can you catch a sailfish on fly in Broome?

Yes. A Broome gameboat runs private fly fishing days for sailfish using tease and switch, where fish are raised to the boat and offered a fly at close range. These trips run May to October, depend on conditions and tides, and book out early.
Is reef fishing for red emperor still open in Broome?

Yes. The West Coast demersal closure doesn't apply in the North West, and tourism bodies note that recreational and charter demersal fishing remains available there. Red emperor, coral trout and bluebone are main targets on Broome reef trips. North Coast bag and size limits changed in June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules.

kimberley.season: Kimberley coast live-aboards run from about April, and Broome-based boats switch to the Rowley Shoals and Scott Reef from late August to November. The Kuri Bay lodge operates from March to January, with the best weather from May to August. Around Kununurra, the dam-regulated Ord River fishes year round. Check road conditions with the Kununurra Visitor Centre.

p: Saltwater crocodiles live in almost every Kimberley waterway that holds barramundi, so stand back from the edge and never clean fish at the water. Big tides drive fishing times along the coast. Some live-aboards warn that Traditional Owner visitor pass fees may be added to trip costs. Some long-running Kununurra day-trip operators have stopped taking fishing bookings, so check with the visitor centre. Check the current DPIRD North Coast barramundi and demersal rules before keeping fish.

faq: How long are Kimberley fishing live-aboards?

Most run about a week or more. For example, Broome-based live-aboards publish nine-day itineraries for up to six anglers, with all meals, accommodation and tackle included. Fly-in lodge stays run four to seven nights.
Can you fish for barramundi around Kununurra?

Yes. The Ord River below the dams and Lake Kununurra fish year round, and the lake has been restocked with more than a million barramundi since 2013. Ivanhoe Crossing and Lily Creek Lagoon are popular land-based spots, but saltwater crocodiles are present, so ask the visitor centre about safe areas.
Where can you fly fish for blue bastards in the Kimberley?

Kuri Bay, a remote pearl-farm lodge about 70 minutes by seaplane from Broome, is known for sight fishing the flats and beaches for blue bastards, golden trevally and big queenfish on fly and lure. Some fly outfits are supplied.
Are there Aboriginal-guided fishing tours in the Kimberley?

Yes. In the East Kimberley, Balanggarra man Sam 'Birchy' Birch runs fishing tours on his family's Country, from full-day catch-and-cook trips and overnight safaris to five- and ten-day 4WD tagalongs from Home Valley Station on the Gibb River Road.

intro: Perth's offshore fishing has changed. Since 16 December 2025, charter fishing for demersal scalefish such as WA dhufish, pink snapper and baldchin groper has been closed in the Perth metropolitan area, and boat-based recreational demersal fishing across the West Coast bioregion stays closed until spring 2027.

What remains is some of the best summer game fishing in southern Australia. Out past Rottnest Island, the deep water of the Perth trench (Rottnest Trench) draws marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo, and private gameboats run there from Hillarys Boat Harbour. Licensed West Coast charters can also offer rock lobster fishing.
perth.season: Charter game fishing in the Perth trench runs from about November to March for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo. Boat-based demersal fishing for dhufish and snapper is closed until spring 2027, and charter demersal fishing in the metro area is closed until then too.

Deep water west of Rottnest for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo

Inshore waters; check Rottnest Island Reserve rules

p: Most Perth fishing charters leave from Hillarys Boat Harbour in the northern suburbs; Fremantle is the other main base.

Under the 2025 reforms, charter demersal fishing is closed in the metro area from 16 December 2025, while charters with demersal tags can keep fishing for demersals elsewhere in the West Coast bioregion under a reduced 25-tonne catch limit. Pink snapper in Cockburn and Warnbro Sounds have a 1 August to 31 January spawning closure. Paying charter guests do not need a boat licence. Check the current DPIRD rules before you go.

faq: Can you still catch dhufish on a Perth fishing charter?

Not in the metro area. Charter fishing for demersal scalefish, including dhufish and pink snapper, has been closed in the Perth metropolitan area since 16 December 2025, and boat-based recreational demersal fishing in the West Coast bioregion is closed until spring 2027.
When is marlin season off Perth?
Perth game fishing charters target the trench off Rottnest from about November to March for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo. Marlin are usually tagged and released.

geraldton.season: Abrolhos live-aboards run from late February to mid May, with weekly Sunday-to-Saturday departures from Geraldton. Rock lobster and day fishing tours from Geraldton are seasonal and depend on the weather. The Abrolhos baldchin groper spawning closure runs 1 October to 31 December. Only charters holding West Coast demersal tags can keep demersal fish, so ask your operator before booking.

p: Live-aboards and day boats leave from Batavia Coast Marina in central Geraldton. Live-aboard guests board at 5pm the evening before departure.

The Abrolhos is in the West Coast bioregion, where boat-based recreational demersal fishing is closed until spring 2027. Licensed charters with demersal tags can still fish for demersals outside the Perth metro area under a 25-tonne annual limit. Since December 2024, licensed West Coast charters can also fish for rock lobster, with an 8-lobster bag limit per passenger. The islands are a Fish Habitat Protection Area with their own rules, so check the current DPIRD rules. Book early: at least one Abrolhos live-aboard was fully booked for 2026 and taking 2027 bookings by late 2026.

faq: Can I keep dhufish on an Abrolhos charter?

Only with an operator that holds West Coast demersal tags. Charter demersal fishing outside the Perth metro area continues under a tag system with a 25-tonne annual limit, and at least one Abrolhos live-aboard says it still targets dhufish, pink snapper and baldchin. Day charters may set their own limits, such as two demersals per person.
How far are the Abrolhos Islands from Geraldton?
About 60 kilometres west. It usually takes around three hours by charter boat to reach the southern Pelsaert Group.
Can you catch rock lobster on a Geraldton charter?

Yes. Geraldton cray tours set and pull pots, and each guest can keep up to eight rock lobsters under the bag limit, with no lobster licence needed on the tour. Abrolhos live-aboards also pull lobster pots daily for dinner.
Can you visit the Abrolhos Islands on a day trip?

Yes, when the weather allows. Geraldton day excursions to the Abrolhos offer either fishing or snorkelling and need at least six passengers. For more time at the islands, most anglers book a six-night live-aboard.

western-australia.season: Go north in the dry season, roughly April to October, for Kimberley barramundi, Broome reef and billfish trips and Montebello live-aboards. Exmouth fishes year round, with Gulf sailfish in October and November and blue marlin from October to April. Abrolhos live-aboards run from late February to mid May, and Perth trench game fishing from November to March.

p: WA's charter fishing splits into three broad zones. In the tropical North West (Broome, the Kimberley and the Pilbara), demersal fishing is still open. On the Coral Coast (Geraldton, Shark Bay and Exmouth), live-aboards and gameboats work islands and the continental shelf. In the south-west, demersal fishing is in a recovery closure, so charters focus on pelagics and rock lobster.

p: DPIRD says paying guests on licensed charter fishing tours do not need a Recreational Fishing from Boat Licence, but recreational rules such as bag and size limits still apply, with an exception for West Coast demersal scalefish. In the West Coast bioregion (Kalbarri to Augusta), boat-based recreational demersal fishing is closed until spring 2027. Charter demersal fishing is closed in the Perth metro area, while tagged charters elsewhere on the West Coast share a 25-tonne annual limit. Since 1 December 2024, licensed West Coast charters can also fish for rock lobster, with an 8-lobster bag limit per passenger. New demersal limits apply in the North Coast and Gascoyne from 1 June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules.

In the Kimberley and Pilbara, saltwater crocodiles live in most rivers, creeks and estuaries that hold barramundi, and tides of eight to nine metres or more change conditions quickly. Book licensed operators who know local tides and marine park zones. Several operators recommend travel insurance, since trips can be cancelled or rescheduled for weather.

faq: Is dhufish fishing open in WA?

Not by boat for recreational anglers in the West Coast bioregion (Kalbarri to Augusta), which is closed until spring 2027. Charter demersal fishing is closed in the Perth metro area, but a few tagged charters elsewhere on the West Coast, such as some Abrolhos live-aboards, still target dhufish. Demersal fishing remains open in the North West.
Where can you do a fishing live-aboard in Western Australia?

Live-aboards run to the Abrolhos Islands from Geraldton, Shark Bay from Denham, and the Montebello Islands from Onslow or Exmouth. Islands off Ningaloo are also fished from Exmouth, and the Kimberley coast, Rowley Shoals and Scott Reef from Broome. Trips run from two days to nine days, and most take between four and twelve guests.
Can you still go on a fishing charter in Perth?

Yes, but not for demersals. Charter fishing for dhufish, pink snapper and other demersal scalefish has been closed in the Perth metro area since 16 December 2025. Perth charters now run summer game fishing for marlin, mahi mahi, tuna and wahoo in the Perth trench off Rottnest.

intro: Hobart's fishing charters work the sheltered water south of the city and the River Derwent estuary. Shared trips from Margate Marina, about 15 minutes south of the CBD, bottom fish around Blackmans Bay, Bonnet Hill and Opossum Bay for flathead, Australian salmon, squid, gurnard perch and wrasse, and suit beginners, families and seniors. Private charters can head offshore into Storm Bay for southern bluefin tuna and striped trumpeter.

Hobart is also a fly fishing base. The lower Derwent estuary holds bream, Australian salmon and sea-run brown trout within minutes of the city, and guides collect anglers from Hobart for day trips to the Derwent Valley rivers and the Central Highlands lakes.
hobart.season: Shared inshore trips target flathead, Australian salmon and squid, while offshore private charters chase tuna and striped trumpeter. Striped trumpeter are closed from 1 September to 31 October, and squid in the south-east region (Lemon Rock to Whale Head) from 15 October to 14 November in 2025 and 2026. Sea-run trout in the Derwent are best from July to September.

p: Boat charters mostly fish inshore reefs and bays south of the city, while trout guides work the Derwent estuary and travel inland.

p: Rod-and-line fishing in Tasmanian marine waters needs no licence, but rock lobster, abalone, scallops, nets and set lines do, and charter clients must hold any licence the activity requires. Anyone 14 or older fishing for trout needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence. Check the current NRE Tas rules for bag and size limits.
Shared boat trips run year-round in mostly calm water, and the 3-hour cruise is usually an afternoon or sunset trip.

faq: Can you catch trout in Hobart itself?

Yes. Sea-run brown trout move through the Derwent estuary, with shore spots from the Tasman Bridge up to the Bridgewater Bridge. One Hobart guide finds late afternoon and evening best, ideally with the tide high or starting to fall. The Derwent below New Norfolk Bridge is an inland water open all year, so an IFS angling licence is needed.
Is there a Hobart fishing trip that combines fishing and diving?

Yes. Diver's Fishing Charters Hobart runs a half-day Hook, Dive and Grill trip from Margate Marina where anglers bottom fish while certified divers explore the same reefs, followed by an onboard barbecue.
Can I go tuna fishing from Hobart?

Yes, by private charter: Diver's Fishing Charters Hobart takes private groups offshore from Margate Marina for southern bluefin tuna and striped trumpeter. Half and full-day charters that also catch tuna run from Eaglehawk Neck on the Tasman Peninsula, about 45 minutes' drive from Hobart Airport.
Is there a short fishing trip in Hobart for visitors with little time?

Yes. Diver's runs a shared 3-hour fishing and sightseeing cruise from Margate Marina with all gear, a skipper and deckhand, drinks and fruit included; children under 6 go free. It usually runs late in the day, with mornings on request.

intro: Pirates Bay at Eaglehawk Neck is the gateway to the Tasman Peninsula's game fishing water, where the state fisheries agency lists bluefin tuna, mako shark and swordfish among the catch. Charter boats launch here and at Port Arthur for southern bluefin, albacore and striped tuna, and bottom fish the deep reefs for striped trumpeter, tiger flathead, jackass morwong and ocean perch.

The peninsula is about 45 minutes' drive from Hobart Airport. On rough days, calmer bay charters fish Frederick Henry Bay from Dodges Ferry for sand flathead, calamari, Australian salmon and whiting, and some boats run reef trips around Maria Island from Dunalley or Orford.
tasman-peninsula.season: Local charters run tuna trips from about March to August. Bottom and reef fishing runs all year, outside the striped trumpeter closure (1 September to 31 October). Yellowtail kingfish and snapper turn up in the bays from November to March.

p: Frederick Henry, Norfolk and Blackman bays are shark refuge areas: no sharks, skates or rays may be taken other than elephantfish. Maori octopus can be caught recreationally in Eaglehawk Bay. Marine rod-and-line fishing needs no licence; check NRE Tas alerts and the current bag limits before you go.

Boats choose their launch point on the day: when Pirates Bay is too rough, operators may switch to Port Arthur or to sheltered Frederick Henry Bay. Pick-ups from Hobart can be arranged with some charters, and at least one pairs trips with local accommodation.

faq: How far is Eaglehawk Neck from Hobart?
About a 45-minute drive from Hobart Airport, on the road to the Port Arthur Historic Site. Dodges Ferry, used for bay charters, is about 15 minutes from the airport.
Can I keep sharks caught around the Tasman Peninsula?
Not in Frederick Henry, Norfolk or Blackman bays, which are shark refuge areas where sharks, skates and rays other than elephantfish cannot be taken. Check NRE Tas rules for other waters.
Can I combine a fishing charter with a visit to Port Arthur?

Yes. Eaglehawk Neck is on the road to the Port Arthur Historic Site, Tasman Spirit Charters' catamaran is moored in Carnarvon Bay at Port Arthur, and Mr Flathead also uses the Port Arthur jetty on Garden Point Road.
What happens if it is too rough off Eaglehawk Neck?

Charters pick the launch point to suit the conditions. Mr Flathead meets at Eaglehawk Neck, Port Arthur or Dodges Ferry depending on the day, and its Dodges Ferry bay charter fishes calmer Frederick Henry Bay for flathead, calamari, salmon and whiting.

intro: Tasmania's Central Highlands is a plateau of more than a thousand lakes, lagoons and tarns (Discover Tasmania puts the count nearer 3,000) holding wild brown trout, and it is the heart of the state's fly fishing. Guides base themselves at Miena on yingina / Great Lake, or collect clients from Hobart, and fish by boat or on foot across Great Lake, Arthurs Lake, Penstock and Little Pine lagoons, Lake Crescent and the remote Western Lakes.

Sight fishing is the local speciality: polaroiding cruising fish, casting to tailing trout on flooded margins and fishing mayfly hatches and gum beetle falls. The weather can swing from calm sun to sleet even in summer, so guides plan several options for each day.
central-highlands.season: Most brown trout waters are open from 1 August 2026 to 2 May 2027, and Great Lake all year except Canal Bay (28 November 2026 to 28 March 2027 only). Rainbow waters open 3 October 2026. Discover Tasmania rates mid-October to mid-April as the best fishing; guides single out beetle season (November-December) and the autumn run (March-April).

p: Anyone 14 or older needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, including guided clients; licences come in 48-hour, 7-day, 28-day, season and five-season versions. Waters flowing into Great Lake, Lake Leake, Arthurs Lake and Dee Lagoon are closed, along with 50 m below where they enter. Trout Weekend runs at the IFS Liawenee Field Station on 10 and 11 October 2026.

Highland weather changes fast, so guides choose the day's water on the morning and keep lower, more sheltered lakes such as Lake Leake or Four Springs in reserve for storms. Pack warm layers: Miena Guiding's kit list includes a warm jacket and jumper.

faq: Can you fish Great Lake in winter?
Yes. Great Lake is open all year except Canal Bay, which opens only from 28 November 2026 to 28 March 2027. Most other highland waters close in early May.
Do I need an angling licence at Currawong Lakes?
No. An angling licence is not needed at registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes, but access fees apply.
How far ahead should I book a Central Highlands guide?

Early. One Miena-based guide business says its peak periods, beetle season in November and December and the autumn run in March and April, book out well ahead, and suggests three to six months for a specific window.
Can I do a Central Highlands guided day from Hobart or Launceston?

Yes, but it makes a long day. Some guides include transport from Hobart; Miena Guiding Tasmania charges extra for Hobart or Launceston transfers and adds about three hours to the day, so arriving in the Highlands the night before is recommended.

intro: Launceston and the Northern Midlands are Tasmania's river country. Guides based in Launceston and at Cressy in the Northern Midlands fish the meadow streams and tailwaters for wild brown and rainbow trout: Brumbys Creek, the South Esk, Macquarie, Meander, North Esk, St Patricks and Mersey rivers, with most water within an hour's drive of accommodation.

Trips are wading or drifting by raft or boat, and many include tuition, so the region suits first-timers as well as experienced dry fly anglers. Longer trips reach the Central Highlands lakes, the Currawong Lakes private fishery, or the Western Lakes wilderness beside the Walls of Jerusalem National Park.
launceston.season: Most rivers are open from 1 August 2026 to 2 May 2027, and the lower sections of Brumbys Creek and the Macquarie, Meander and South Esk rivers stay open until 30 May 2027. One local river guide says dry fly fishing becomes the norm after early October. The kanamaluka / Tamar below the Charles Street and West Tamar Road bridges is open all year.

p: Every angler aged 14 or over needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, and some guides can sell one. Registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes don't require a licence but charge access fees. Launceston has direct flights from Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.
Guides price per angler or per group, and Trout Territory and Tasmania Fly Fishing both list separate rates for non-fishing partners.

faq: Can I do a half-day fly fishing trip from Launceston?
Yes. Tasmania Fly Fishing runs private half days (8.30am-12.30pm or 1.30-5.30pm) on rivers, streams and small lakes close to Launceston, aimed at beginners and visitors short on time.
Which Launceston-area rivers stay open after the main season closes?
The lower sections of Brumbys Creek and the Macquarie, Meander and South Esk rivers stay open until 30 May 2027, four weeks after most waters close.
Can a non-fishing partner join a Launceston fly fishing tour?
Usually, for a fee. Tasmania Fly Fishing charges non-fishing guests $100 to $150 depending on trip length, and Trout Territory charges non-angling companions $250 per person per day.
Is there estuary fishing near Launceston?
Yes. The kanamaluka / Tamar estuary below the Charles Street and West Tamar Road bridges is open all year, and Trout Territory runs estuary days there on fly, lure or bait.

p: Tasmania's charter and guide industry splits into salt water in the south-east and east, and trout country inland. Boats work out of Hobart and the Tasman Peninsula, with East Coast charters at St Helens, while professional trout guides operate from Hobart, Miena in the Central Highlands, Launceston and Cressy.

Inshore bottom fishing for flathead, salmon and squid, offshore tuna and striped trumpeter, and Derwent estuary fly fishing
Tasman Peninsula
Pirates Bay and Port Arthur for southern bluefin and albacore tuna, deep reef fishing and calmer bay trips
St Helens & the East Coast
Georges Bay and offshore grounds for flathead, bream, salmon, tuna and mako shark; charters fish inside the bay and offshore
Central Highlands
