Midlands rivers such as Brumbys Creek, the South Esk and Meander for river fly fishing

p: Salt water fishes all year, with tuna off the Tasman Peninsula from about March to August. Striped trumpeter are closed from 1 September to 31 October. Most trout waters open on 1 August 2026 and close on 2 May 2027; Great Lake and several lowland waters stay open all year.

Rod-and-line fishing in Tasmanian marine waters needs no licence; rock lobster, abalone, scallops, nets and set lines do, and NRE Tas says charter clients must hold any licence the activity requires. Inland, everyone 14 or older needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, guided clients included; 48-hour, 7-day and 28-day licences are available, junior licences (14-17) are free, and some guides sell them. Registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes need no licence.

faq: When does the Tasmanian trout season open?

Most waters open on the first Saturday in August (1 August 2026) and close on the Sunday nearest 30 April (2 May 2027). Designated rainbow trout waters run from 3 October 2026 to 30 May 2027, and some waters, including Great Lake, are open all year.
Can I combine sea fishing and trout fishing on one Tasmanian trip?

Yes. Hobart has both: shared and private boat trips from Margate Marina, and fly fishing guides who work the Derwent estuary or drive to the Central Highlands. Eaglehawk Neck's tuna and reef charters are about 45 minutes from Hobart Airport, and guides at Miena or Launceston cover the highland lakes and northern rivers.
Which part of Tasmania suits beginners on a fly fishing trip?

Launceston and the Northern Midlands rivers are within about an hour of accommodation and several guides there run half days and tuition, which suits first-timers. Hobart-based guides also take beginners, starting with a casting lesson.
intro: Tasmania combines cold-water ocean fishing with what Discover Tasmania calls one of the world's great trout fisheries. Charters work Storm Bay south of Hobart, the Tasman Peninsula and the East Coast, where Discover Tasmania calls St Helens the state's saltwater sport-fishing capital. Professional guides take anglers to the lakes of the Central Highlands and the rivers of the north.

Saltwater trips target southern bluefin tuna, striped trumpeter, flathead and squid; inland guides specialise in sight fishing for wild brown and rainbow trout, from Launceston and Cressy, Miena on Great Lake and Hobart.
tasmania.season: Saltwater fishing runs all year, with tuna off the Tasman Peninsula from about March to August. Most trout waters are open from 1 August 2026 to 2 May 2027, and Discover Tasmania rates mid-October to mid-April as the best trout fishing. Striped trumpeter are closed 1 September to 31 October.

intro: Port Phillip is Melbourne's home water: a big, mostly sheltered bay ringed by boat ramps from St Kilda and Black Rock round to Carrum, Mornington, Sorrento and Queenscliff, with Geelong's Corio Bay in the west. Charter boats fish the bay for snapper, King George whiting, flathead and calamari, and the bigger boats head out through the Heads into Bass Strait for gummy shark, kingfish and tuna when the weather allows.

Most Melbourne charters are shared trips of four to five hours, so you can book a single seat or the whole boat. Several operators trailer their boats and choose the ramp a few days out, depending on where the fish are, so confirm the departure point after you book. In the peak snapper weeks, boats run early-morning, midday and evening sessions.
port-phillip.season: Spring is the drawcard. Melbourne operators run their main snapper season from about October to December, some extending it into January or April, with three sessions a day at the peak. Whiting and calamari fish well most of the year, gummy sharks are a cooler-season target from Queenscliff (late April to mid-July), and kingfish and tuna turn up outside the Heads from about mid-January to early April.

p: Bay trips work the reefs, grass beds and sand flats around the edge of Port Phillip, moving with the season and the weather. Queenscliff boats sit right at the Heads, so they can fish the bay or, in good conditions, Bass Strait.

faq: Can I book a single seat on a Melbourne snapper charter?

Yes. Most Port Phillip operators sell individual places on shared trips as well as whole-boat charters, and some will fill the boat with other anglers. Snapper trips can need a minimum number of people to go ahead, so book early in peak season.
Which ramp will my Port Phillip charter leave from?

It often isn't fixed until a few days before. Operators such as Pro Red, Unreel and Cassar move between Carrum, St Kilda, Mornington, Hastings and other ramps to follow the fish, and confirm the meeting point after booking.
Are Port Phillip charters suitable for children?

Many are. Geelong Fishing Charters runs family trips where under-10s fish free, and bay trips generally welcome children from about five or six, but offshore Bass Strait trips usually have a minimum age of 12.
Can I fish for snapper after work in Melbourne?

Yes, in season. Unreel runs a 4pm to 9pm snapper session from its Port Phillip ramps, and Gone Fishing runs a five-hour evening snapper charter from Queenscliff between about 1 November and mid-December.
Do Melbourne charters go outside Port Phillip Heads?

Some do. Queenscliff boats such as Gone Fishing head into Bass Strait for kingfish and tuna from mid-January to early April, and for snapper and sharks when the weather suits. Everyone wears a life jacket crossing the Heads.

intro: Western Port lies just east of Port Phillip, wrapped around French Island and Phillip Island, with strong tidal currents and deep channels. Hastings is the charter hub, with boats leaving the Hastings boat ramp and Western Port Marina, and Stony Point and San Remo also used. The bay is known for big spring snapper, King George whiting, and gummy sharks in the channels.

Hastings is also the main launch for Melbourne's offshore trips into Bass Strait, where charters chase kingfish, southern bluefin tuna and mako sharks. Boats range from trailered catamarans for six to eight anglers to a 15 metre vessel that takes groups of up to 20 and runs every day of the year.
western-port.season: Snapper move into Western Port in spring, and operators fish them from about September or October, with Hastings often firing early before the run moves into Port Phillip. Twilight snapper sessions run from Hastings in season. Whiting is reliable for much of the year, best from about October to May. Gummy sharks are caught year-round, and offshore kingfish and tuna trips run mostly from summer into autumn.

p: Tides drive the fishing here: skippers time trips around the tide changes and fish the channels and banks around the islands.

faq: Is Western Port or Port Phillip better for snapper?

Both get a spring run. Several operators start the season at Hastings in Western Port and shift to Port Phillip ramps such as Carrum as the run moves up the bay, choosing a few days out based on where fish are biting.
Can I go offshore into Bass Strait from Hastings?

Yes. Hastings is the usual departure for offshore trips targeting kingfish, southern bluefin tuna and sharks. Trips run up to about eight hours, depend on the weather, and usually have a minimum age of 12. Westernport Fishing Charters also runs a ten-hour trip that combines the bay and Bass Strait.
Can a big group charter one boat on Western Port?

Yes. Westernport Fishing Charters' 15 m Flying Fish 2 takes private groups of up to 20 from Western Port Marina, priced by the hour with a four-hour minimum, and suits clubs, work groups and bucks parties.

intro: Portland, in Victoria's far south-west, is the state's best-known southern bluefin tuna port. Nutrient-rich water from the Bonney Upwelling and a short run to deep water bring tuna, sharks and big reef fish within reach, and in autumn and winter many Melbourne charter boats join the local fleet. Port Fairy, about an hour east, is the other main base, and Warrnambool is used when the weather suits.

Local skippers fish all year, bottom-bouncing for snapper, gummy shark, flathead and nannygai and running trips out to the continental shelf for deep-water species such as blue-eye trevalla and hapuku. Tuna days are long, often eight to ten hours, so expect a full day offshore and pack for cold, rough conditions.
portland.season: Bluefin tuna are the main event from about March to August. Local operators quote May to August for tuna trips, Melbourne operators list school fish from about April to July and big 'barrel' fish from March to October, and some run Portland trips from May to September. Kingfish are a summer target, especially around Port Fairy, and reef and shelf fishing runs all year.

faq: How far offshore do Portland tuna charters go?
Often a long way. Bluefin are frequently found well offshore, sometimes over the continental shelf, so tuna charters are usually full days of about eight to ten hours.
Do Melbourne charter operators fish Portland?
Yes. Several Melbourne operators, including Pro Red, Unreel, Cassar and Sharkmen, run seasonal bluefin tuna trips out of Portland, alongside local Portland and Port Fairy boats.
Is Port Fairy a good alternative to Portland?
Yes. Port Fairy has its own charter boats that chase tuna, sharks and kingfish, and some will launch from Portland or Warrnambool depending on the weather and where the fish are.
Can I go deep-sea reef fishing from the South West when tuna aren't running?

Yes. Port Fairy's Salty Dog Charters makes regular trips to the continental shelf for deep-water species, and Unreel runs full-day deep-reef trips from Port Fairy and Portland, sometimes using electric reels.

intro: Lakes Entrance sits where the Gippsland Lakes meet Bass Strait, and it is the jumping-off point for East Gippsland's offshore fishing. Charter boats cross the bar from the Skate Park ramp to grounds about 20 to 40 minutes out, targeting snapper, gummy shark and flathead, with mako sharks, tuna and marlin possible on longer trips for boats surveyed to 100 nautical miles.

Behind the entrance, the Gippsland Lakes are Australia's largest coastal lake system and one of Victoria's best bream and dusky flathead fisheries, from Lake King, Metung and Paynesville up into the Mitchell, Nicholson and Tambo rivers. Just east, Lake Tyers is known for sight fishing big flathead on its shallow flats. Small-boat lure guides work both, for up to three anglers.
gippsland.season: Snapper are caught off Lakes Entrance all year, with pinkies arriving in numbers from about May and some of the state's biggest snapper landed between October and April. Gummy sharks build as the water warms towards summer. In the lakes and Lake Tyers, bream and flathead fish well through the warmer months, when flathead sit on the shallows, and crabbing is best from about October to January.

faq: Do Lakes Entrance charters fish the lakes or the ocean?

Both are available. Far Out Charters fishes offshore in Bass Strait for snapper, gummy shark and flathead, while East Gippsland Sportfishing runs guided lure trips inside the Gippsland Lakes and on Lake Tyers for bream and flathead.
How long is the run to the fishing grounds from Lakes Entrance?
Usually short. Far Out Charters says most trips take about 20 to 40 minutes to reach the grounds after crossing the bar.
Is Lake Tyers good for flathead?
Yes. Lake Tyers is known for big dusky flathead, with fish over a metre possible, and guides sight fish them on the shallow sand flats with soft plastics, paddle tails and swimbaits.
Can beginners join a guided lure-fishing trip on the Gippsland Lakes?
Yes. Guides teach knots, casting and how to work soft plastics and hard-body lures, and the Gippsland Lakes are described as the easiest East Gippsland system for first-time charter clients.

intro: The Murray forms Victoria's northern border and is the heartland of Murray cod fishing. Lake Mulwala, created by Yarrawonga Weir, is one of the country's top cod fisheries, where fish breed naturally among the drowned timber of the old river bed, and the river downstream towards Echuca and Swan Hill also holds big cod. Lake Mulwala and the area around Yarrawonga also hold trout cod, a rarer native species.

Guided trips are small-boat lure fishing for one to three anglers, using surface lures, swimbaits and modern sonar to find fish. Lake Mulwala and the Murray itself are New South Wales waters, so check which licence and rules apply before you fish; Lake Hume, upstream, is the one stretch where a Victorian licence is valid.
murray-river.season: Murray cod can be fished from December to August. The closed season runs from 1 September to 30 November, and the river from Yarrawonga Weir to Tocumwal is closed to all fishing during that time. Summer mornings and evenings suit active fish, winter is the time for trophy cod, and golden perch are a good target in spring.

faq: Is Lake Mulwala in Victoria or New South Wales?
The lake sits between Yarrawonga in Victoria and Mulwala in NSW, but it is classified as NSW water, so a NSW recreational fishing licence applies whether you fish from a boat, kayak or the shore.
Can I fish for Murray cod in spring?

Not for cod in most waters: the closed season runs 1 September to 30 November, and the Murray from Yarrawonga Weir to Tocumwal is closed to all fishing then. Guides switch to golden perch during the closure.
How many people can go on a guided Murray cod trip?
Usually one to three. Lake Mulwala Sportfishing says one to three anglers is ideal in its bass boat and asks you to get in touch about a fourth.

intro: Lake Eildon and the High Country around Mansfield combine a big lake known for trophy Murray cod and golden perch with some of Victoria's most scenic trout water. Mountain rivers such as the Delatite, Howqua, Jamieson, King and upper Goulburn are fished on foot by fly anglers, while below the dam the Goulburn River around Thornton and Alexandra is big enough to fish from a drift boat.

Guiding here is usually one guide to one or two anglers, with rods, flies and waders supplied, so you don't need your own gear. Mansfield guides run walk-and-wade trout days and summer Murray cod drifts, and the Goulburn Valley's guides have run drift boats, lessons and beginner weekends since 1994. Guided river fishing is mostly catch and release.
eildon.season: Lake Eildon has no Murray cod closed season, so cod can be chased there all year, though more are caught in the warmer months. In rivers, cod follow the statewide closure from 1 September to 30 November, and guided cod drift trips run December to April. Trout rivers have their own season; Goulburn beginner workshops run monthly from November to May. Check the current VFA rules.

faq: Do I need fly-fishing experience for a guided High Country trip?

No. Guides take first-timers through to experienced anglers, with tuition included and waders, boots, rods and flies supplied. Goulburn Valley Fly Fishing also runs a two-day beginner workshop in Alexandra.
Is there phone reception on High Country rivers?
Often not. Back of Beyond Fly Fishing notes most locations have no mobile coverage, gives indicative pick-up and drop-off times, and carries a satellite messenger with SOS.
Can I fish the Goulburn River from a boat?

Yes, with a guide. Goulburn Valley Fly Fishing Centre runs private half- and full-day drift-boat trips for one or two anglers, with the guide rowing so you can fish banks that can't be reached on foot.

intro: Victoria packs a lot of fishing into a small state. Melbourne's two bays, Port Phillip and Western Port, are famous for the spring snapper run and King George whiting, while Bass Strait offers sharks, kingfish and tuna. Portland in the far south-west is the bluefin tuna capital, Lakes Entrance opens onto East Gippsland's reefs and lakes, and inland the Murray and Lake Eildon are Murray cod country.

Melbourne's bay boats leave from Carrum, St Kilda, Mornington, Queenscliff, Geelong and Hastings, so a charter can be a day trip from the city. Further afield, Portland and Port Fairy anchor the far west, Lakes Entrance the east, Yarrawonga the Murray, and Mansfield the High Country fly-fishing guides.
victoria.season: Spring (October to December) is snapper season in Melbourne's bays, summer brings kingfish and mako sharks, and autumn into winter is bluefin tuna time at Portland and Port Fairy. Murray cod are closed from 1 September to 30 November in most waters, but Lake Eildon stays open all year.

Lake Mulwala and the Murray are NSW waters, where NSW rules and a NSW licence apply; Lake Hume is the exception, where a Victorian licence is valid. Bag and size limits change, so check the current VFA rules.

faq: Which part of Victoria should I base a fishing charter trip in?

It depends on the target. Melbourne's bays suit snapper, whiting and family trips close to the city; Portland and Port Fairy are the bases for bluefin tuna; Lakes Entrance offers offshore reef fishing; and Yarrawonga and Mansfield are the bases for guided Murray cod and trout.
Where can I catch southern bluefin tuna in Victoria?

Portland and Port Fairy in the south-west are the main tuna ports, from about March to August. Several Melbourne operators move boats there for the season, and Hastings and Queenscliff boats also run offshore tuna trips into Bass Strait early in the year.
Can I fish for Murray cod in Victoria during spring?

In most rivers and lakes, no: the cod closed season runs 1 September to 30 November. Lake Eildon, Eildon Pondage and a handful of other lakes have no closed season, so cod can be targeted there all year.

faq: What is the best North Coast port for a fishing charter?

It depends on the trip. Evans Head suits anglers after deep-water pearl perch, Yamba has the most choice of shared and private reef trips, Brunswick Heads runs full days close to Byron Bay, and Tweed Heads is the closest to Gold Coast Airport, with reefs only about 3 km from the river entrance.
When is game fishing season on the NSW North Coast?
Mainly summer. Tweed Heads boats chase marlin, wahoo, mahi mahi, mackerel and tuna from about December to March, and the warmer months bring the same pelagics off Byron and Evans Head.
Do North Coast fishing charters cross a bar?

Yes. Tweed Heads boats cross the Tweed bar, Byron Bay Charters runs from Brunswick Heads and confirms each trip the night before once sea and bar conditions are checked, and Yamba boats cross the Clarence River bar with life jackets worn during the crossing.

Yes, outside the sanctuary zones. The Solitary Islands Marine Park stretches from Coffs Harbour to the Sandon River, and Coffs Harbour charters run small-group trips to South Solitary Island for kingfish, cobia, jewfish, snapper and pearl perch, with mackerel, marlin and wahoo in season.
Why is South West Rocks good for game fishing?

The continental shelf is only about 12 nautical miles off Laggers Point, one of its closest points to the NSW coast, so warm current and pelagics such as black marlin, wahoo and mahi mahi can come very close to shore.
What can you do if it's too rough offshore on the Mid North Coast?

Head for a river. Port Macquarie guides fish the Hastings, Maria, Macleay and Manning rivers, and South West Rocks guides can switch to the Macleay River estuary for flathead, mulloway, bream, whiting and mangrove jack.

items: Port Stephens (Nelson Bay, Corlette, Soldiers Point)
Marlin at the FADs about 20 km out and the Big Gibber, reef fishing around Cabbage Tree and Broughton islands, and a big sheltered estuary
Newcastle and Lake Macquarie
Small-boat lure guiding on the Hunter River from Tomago, and private trips on Lake Macquarie from Kilaben Bay for flathead and mulloway
Terrigal
Reef boats from The Haven for snapper, jewfish and kingfish, and game trips to Browns Mountain and the Norah Head Canyons
Hardys Bay (Broken Bay)
Bouddi Peninsula reefs, or calm water inside Broken Bay when it's windy; fishing charters run December to April

p: This region has some of the state's best short trips for kids. Port Stephens boats run sheltered family mornings near Cabbage Tree Island and Fingal, Capn's Charters runs three-hour calm-water kids' sessions on the Hunter River, and Terrigal Fishing Tours runs Young Guns trips from Hardys Bay.

Port Stephens is a marine park and Lake Macquarie hasn't been commercially netted since 2002; zoning and NSW bag limits apply. Shared trips usually need minimum numbers (five on one Central Coast boat), so wait for confirmation before booking accommodation. Most charters include licence cover.

faq: Where is the best place for marlin near Sydney?

Port Stephens, about 2.5 hours north. Light-tackle boats fish the FADs about 20 km out for black and striped marlin and mahi mahi from December to March, blue marlin trips go over the shelf from January to March, and black marlin sometimes push in to the Big Gibber.
Is there calm-water fishing for kids near Newcastle?

Yes. Capn's Charters runs a three-hour kids' charter on the Hunter River for three children aged 6 to 16 (or two kids and an adult), and Day Trippin Charters fishes sheltered Lake Macquarie with up to four guests.
Can I do a fishing day trip from Sydney to the Central Coast?
Yes. Terrigal is about an hour's drive north of Sydney via the M1 and the Gosford exit, and reef charters from The Haven run about seven and a half hours, leaving at 6 am.

items: Wollongong and Kiama
Big shared reef boats from Belmore Basin, game and overnight trips, and deep-sea trips to 400 m off Kiama
Jervis Bay and Greenwell Point
Squid and snapper in a marine-park bay, offshore reefs, and game and deep-water trips for groups up to 12
Batemans Bay, Narooma and Bermagui
Bay reefs and the Tollgate Islands, Montague Island about 9 km off Narooma, and Bermagui's deep-water grounds
Merimbula and Eden
Short reef trips from Merimbula, kingfish south of Eden from about November to June, and Eden's long game season

p: The South Coast is the state's deep-drop country. Kiama Charter Service fishes the shelf about 30 km out in up to 400 m from May to September, Game On Charters runs full-day deep-drop trips from Batemans Bay with electric reels, and FishBermi targets gemfish and blue-eye trevalla from Bermagui. For game fish, Narooma's season runs from about Christmas to June and Eden's from November to the end of July.

Jervis Bay and Batemans are marine parks with zoning rules that skippers follow. Humpback whales pass close to shore from about May to November, and several operators also run whale-watching trips. Most South Coast charters include licence cover, and shared reef seats cost about $100 for three hours at Merimbula to $240 for a five-hour trip at Batemans Bay.

faq: Where can you go deep-drop fishing on the NSW South Coast?

Kiama Charter Service runs deep-sea trips to the shelf about 30 km out, in water up to 400 m, from May to September. Game On Charters runs full-day deep-drop trips from Batemans Bay, and FishBermi in Bermagui targets gemfish and blue-eye trevalla.
When is game fishing season on the South Coast?

It runs later the further south you go: about December to April off Wollongong, December to June off Narooma, and November to the end of July at Eden, where January to late March is often best for marlin.
Which South Coast port has no bar crossing?
Eden. Twofold Bay is one of the deepest natural harbours in the Southern Hemisphere and has no bar to cross, so Eden charters can head out in conditions that keep bar ports closed.
Are there short fishing trips for families on the South Coast?

Yes. Merimbula has three-hour reef trips from about $100 per adult, with family tickets at Fishpen Charters, and Aquilla Fishing Charters in Wollongong runs two-hour Junior Angler sessions for kids aged 8 to 16 in the school holidays.

top-end.summary: Top End fishing charters are mostly based in Darwin: harbour and offshore trips leave Cullen Bay, Stokes Hill Wharf and Dinah Beach, and barra guides drive guests to the Mary River, Dundee Beach, the Daly and Kakadu. The March–May run-off is peak barramundi time. Shared days cost about $225–$750 per person; private boats about $1,200–$3,540.
intro: The Top End is the northern tip of the Northern Territory, and most NT charter fishing happens within a day's drive of Darwin. Harbour and bluewater boats leave from Cullen Bay, Stokes Hill Wharf and Dinah Beach, while barramundi guides collect guests from Darwin hotels before dawn and drive them to the Mary River billabongs, Shoal Bay, Bynoe Harbour or the Adelaide River.

Further out, Dundee Beach (about 90 minutes from Darwin) is the base for reef and sportfishing on the Dundee Coast, the Daly River is a recreational-only barra river about 2.5 hours south-west, Kakadu's Alligator rivers are fished by a few licensed guides from Jabiru, and the Tiwi Islands are reached by day boat from Leaders Creek or by charter flight to a lodge.
top-end.season: The run-off (about March to May) is the classic time for trophy barramundi on the Mary, Daly and Alligator rivers. The dry season (about May to September) brings stable weather for reef and pelagic trips and billabong barra. The build-up (about September to December) is hot but produces big barra, and calm days off Darwin suit sailfish. Golden snapper and black jewfish bite year-round.

p: Each Top End destination suits a different style of trip, from a half day in Darwin Harbour to a week on a mothership.
items: Darwin
Harbour barra, mud crabs and reef fish on half days; offshore reefs 20–50 km out for black jewfish, golden snapper and Spanish mackerel
Mary River and Shady Camp
The best-known run-off barra water in the Top End, plus Corroboree Billabong day trips about 1.5 hours from Darwin
Kakadu
Only licensed guides may run fishing tours in the park; the Alligator rivers in the run-off and the upper East Alligator in the dry
Daly River
Reserved for recreational fishing, with day charters from the local ramp, Anson Bay runs and liveaboard trips from Darwin
Dundee Beach and Bynoe Harbour
Finniss River barra and the Dundee Coast's reefs out to the Peron Islands; several operators have their own accommodation
Tiwi Islands
Bathurst and Melville islands, about 80 km north of Darwin; reef, bluewater and estuary fishing by day boat or fly-in lodge

sections.h: Trip styles and how far you travel
p: Day trips are the most common way to fish the Top End. Barra day tours generally pick up from Darwin accommodation between about 4:30 and 5am and return mid to late afternoon, while harbour and bluewater trips meet at the wharf or ramp at a time set by the tide.

Multi-day options include Shady Camp run-off packages based at a lodge, Dundee Beach houses and retreats, Kakadu trips staying in Jabiru, liveaboard motherships on the Daly, Mary or Tiwi coasts, and fly-in lodges on the Tiwi Islands.
items: Corroboree Billabong
About 108 km from Darwin
Dundee Beach
About 90 minutes by sealed road
Shady Camp (Mary River)
About 200 km, roughly 1 hour 40 minutes by car
Daly River
About 210–223 km south-west, roughly 2.5 hours
Jabiru (Kakadu)
About 2.5 hours' drive
Leaders Creek (for the Tiwi Islands)
About an hour's drive, then the boat run north

p: You don't need a recreational fishing licence in the Northern Territory, but bag and size limits apply and some areas have their own rules, such as the Mary River fish management zone and a seasonal closure on the lower tidal Daly River (1 October to 31 January, according to NT tourism). Check the current NT Fisheries rules or the free NT Fishing Mate app before keeping fish.

Kakadu needs a Parks Australia pass and Mary River National Park an NT Parks Visitor Pass. The Tiwi Islands are Aboriginal land, and access needs a permit, which guided trips usually include. Saltwater crocodiles live in almost every Top End waterway: never swim, and keep well back from the water's edge.

faq: Can you fish the Top End in the wet season?

Yes, but options narrow. Darwin Harbour and offshore trips run when the weather allows, and wet-season bookings with some operators carry weather-related reschedule terms. Most Tiwi operators and many remote camps close, and Kakadu's fishing guides mostly stop, though NT tourism notes Yellow Water can still be fished.
Which Top End destination is best for a first barramundi trip?

A Corroboree Billabong or Darwin Harbour day trip is the simplest start: several Darwin guides include hotel pick-up and supply all tackle. For a better chance of a fish over a metre, many anglers book a multi-day run-off trip at Shady Camp on the Mary River or on the Daly between March and May.
How far ahead should I book a Top End run-off trip?

Early. The run-off lasts roughly March to May and only about two tide cycles a month suit it, so operators such as Humbug Fishing say the best dates fill quickly. Ask your guide which tides they recommend before booking flights.
Is it cheaper to share a Top End charter or book privately?

Sharing is cheaper per head: Darwin harbour half days start at about $225 per person and barra days out of Darwin are about $400–$750. Private boats cost about $1,200–$1,600 for a half day and $1,900–$3,540 for a full day, which can work out similar for a full group of four to six.
Which Top End fishing trips suit families with children?

Darwin Harbour half days are the easiest: Darwin Harbour Fishing Charters sells a family charter for two adults and three children, and Barra Private Tours takes children from age 5 on half and full days. Barra days to the Mary River start with a 4:30–5am pick-up, and multi-day trips often set minimum ages, such as 8 with Barra Private Tours.

arnhem-land-and-gulf.summary: Fishing in Arnhem Land and the NT Gulf is mostly fly-in. Day charters from Nhulunbuy (Gove) cost $350–$595 per person, while all-inclusive trips to the Cobourg Peninsula, Dhipirri Lodge on the Glyde River, Groote Eylandt or a Gove mothership run 3–7 days from about $4,900 per person. Barramundi peak March–June; reef and bluewater fish suit the dry season.
intro: East of Kakadu, the Northern Territory coast turns into Arnhem Land and then runs south into the Gulf of Carpentaria. This is permit country with few roads, so most visiting anglers fish here on a guided trip: a day charter out of Nhulunbuy on the Gove Peninsula, a fly-in camp or lodge on the Cobourg Peninsula or in East Arnhem, or an all-inclusive package on Groote Eylandt.

The fishing ranges from barramundi and threadfin salmon in the tidal rivers of Arnhem and Buckingham bays and the Glyde River, to coral trout, golden snapper, red emperor, Spanish mackerel and giant trevally on the reefs and islands. In the Gulf, the waters south of Groote Eylandt are known for marlin and sailfish, and the McArthur River at King Ash Bay is a self-drive barra base.
arnhem-land-and-gulf.season: Barramundi peak in the run-off, around March to June on the Glyde River, and Arnhem lodges fish from about March to December. Reef and bluewater species are targeted through the dry season. Camping on the Cobourg Peninsula is limited to May to October. Marlin and sailfish south of Groote Eylandt run mainly from November to March, and McArthur River barra fish best in the build-up and run-off.

items: Cobourg Peninsula and Port Essington
Fly-in fishing camp in Garig Gunak Barlu National Park, better known for bluewater species than barra
Gove Peninsula (Nhulunbuy)
Reef, island and offshore day charters for coral trout, golden snapper, red emperor and Spanish mackerel; Bremer Island trips
Glyde River and the Crocodile Islands
Fly-in lodge barra fishing in East Arnhem, reached by charter flight from Darwin or Gove
Groote Eylandt
Lodge-based reef, bluewater and estuary fishing from Alyangula, with billfish to the south
McArthur River and the Sir Edward Pellew Islands
Mangrove river barra and island reefs from King Ash Bay, about 50 km past Borroloola
Roper River
Big tidal river navigable for about 170 km, with barra sight-cast on the flats

p: Flights do most of the work. Airnorth flies Darwin to Gove in about 1 hour 15 minutes and also serves Groote Eylandt, while lodges and camps on the Cobourg and in East Arnhem are reached by light aircraft, so luggage limits are tight (often 10–15 kg in a soft bag). Borroloola, the gateway to the McArthur River, is about 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin.

Arnhem Land and Groote Eylandt are Aboriginal land, and entering it, including the intertidal waters, needs a written permit from the relevant land council or ranger group; guided operators usually arrange or include them. Nhulunbuy needs a general visitor permit. The Northern Land Council issues recreational fishing permits for set zones, but in November 2026 its online recreation applications were temporarily unavailable, with a paper application pack instead.

Parts of Arnhem Land are dry areas, and takeaway alcohol in Nhulunbuy needs a permit, so ask your operator what is allowed. Saltwater crocodiles are found throughout. Check the current NT Fisheries rules for limits.

faq: Do I need a permit to fish in Arnhem Land?

Usually yes. All of East Arnhem Land is Aboriginal land, and visitors need permits to be there; Nhulunbuy needs a general permit. Most fly-in lodges, camps and charters arrange the permits their guests need, so check what your package includes when you book.
What is the difference between fishing Gove and a fly-in Arnhem Land lodge?

Gove (Nhulunbuy) is a town with an airport, hotels and day charters, so you can fish half or full days and stay in town. Fly-in lodges and camps, such as those on the Cobourg Peninsula or the Glyde River, are all-inclusive multi-day packages reached only by charter flight.
Can you catch billfish in Arnhem Land and the Gulf?
Yes. NT tourism says the waters south of Groote Eylandt hold large numbers of marlin and sailfish, mainly from November to March, and Groote Eylandt Lodge's safaris include trolling for them.
Can I drive to fish the NT Gulf of Carpentaria?

Yes, to the McArthur River. Borroloola is about 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin, and King Ash Bay, about 50 km further on, has a fishing club with a boat ramp, camping, fuel and a mini-mart. Groote Eylandt and the Arnhem Land lodges are fly-in only.
What do all-inclusive Arnhem Land and Groote fishing packages include?

Usually flights from Darwin, transfers, accommodation, meals, guiding, tackle and permits. Groote Eylandt Lodge's 2–5 day packages include Airnorth flights and twin-share rooms, and Cobourg Fishing Safaris includes Darwin transfers, charter flights, park permits, meals and tackle. Drinks policies differ because parts of Arnhem Land are dry areas.

items: Gold Coast
Boats leave the Spit at Main Beach or Runaway Bay Marina; half days fish reefs about 10-20 km out, full days 10-35 km out in 50-95 m
Brisbane and Moreton Bay
Mostly full days from Manly or Sandstone Point, crossing the bay to the Point Lookout reefs, Cape Moreton and Flinders Reef
Sunshine Coast
Noosa, Mooloolaba and Caloundra boats fish Sunshine Reef, North Reef and Chardons Reef out to the Barwon Banks and the Hards

p: Run times differ a lot across the region. Gold Coast half-day reefs are 15-30 minutes from the Seaway, while Brisbane boats need about 1 hour 15 minutes to reach the grounds beyond the South Passage bar, which is why most Brisbane offshore trips are full days.
items: Gold Coast inshore and wider reefs
Snapper, pearl perch, teraglin, tuskfish, cobia and mackerel; black marlin can turn up about 6 km out
Point Lookout reefs and the Cathedrals
Canyons and drop-offs off North Stradbroke Island for snapper, pearl perch, kingfish and amberjack
Cape Moreton, Deep Tempest and Square Patch
Snapper and pearl perch grounds off the northern end of Moreton Island
Flinders Reef and Hutchinsons Shoals
Further reefs and shoals worked by Manly-based boats
Barwon Banks
A reef system about 23 km long, 40 km+ off Caloundra, for pearl perch, snapper, red emperor, amberjack and kingfish
Sunshine Reef, North Reef and Chardons Reef
Noosa's half-day and winter snapper grounds, about 30-45 minutes from the bar
The Hards
Wide grounds in 50-100 m reached on nine- and 12-hour trips from Noosa and Caloundra

p: If the bar is rough or you have young children, calm-water charters stay inside on sheltered estuaries and bays.
items: Gold Coast Broadwater, Nerang River and Jumpinpin
Flathead, whiting, bream, tarwhine, mangrove jack, tailor and trevally
Pumicestone Passage
Behind Bribie Island, fished from Sandstone Point and Pelican Waters, for flathead, bream, whiting and tailor
Moreton Bay and the Brisbane River
Lure fishing for snapper, flathead, jewfish and threadfin salmon on small private boats
Noosa River
Flathead, bream and mangrove jack in the river and its lakes

p: Shared offshore trips across the region usually run five, seven or nine hours, with 12-hour trips from Caloundra and Mooloolaba. Published 2026 prices start at about $200-$245 per person for a five-hour shared reef trip and $320-$360 for a full day, while whole-boat private charters start from $1,840 for a Gold Coast half day for eight anglers. Calm-water family trips start from about $109 per person.

Bars decide whether trips go, so most operators confirm the afternoon or evening before and may cancel at short notice. Rain on its own rarely stops a trip; strong wind and swell do. Catch handling varies: some crews clean and bag fish, others keep them whole, so bring an esky and leave it in the car.

Moreton Bay is a zoned marine park (Scarborough Reef is a yellow zone and Scotts Point a green zone), and Noosa operators point anglers to Great Sandy Marine Park zoning. Queensland has no general recreational fishing licence for tidal waters, but size and possession limits apply on every boat.

faq: Can you reach the reef on a half-day charter in South East Queensland?

Yes, on the Gold Coast and Sunshine Coast. Gold Coast half days fish reefs about 10-20 km out, 15-30 minutes from the Seaway, and Noosa half days fish Sunshine Reef and North Reef about 30-45 minutes away. From Brisbane the run beyond the South Passage bar is longer, so most offshore trips there are full days.
Where can families fish in calm water in South East Queensland?

The Gold Coast Broadwater, the Pumicestone Passage behind Bribie Island and Moreton Bay are the main calm-water options. Charters from Runaway Bay, Sandstone Point and Pelican Waters run short trips for flathead, bream and whiting, and some offer child prices.
When is snapper season in South East Queensland?

Snapper are caught all year, but the bigger fish and best bites are in the cooler months from late autumn through winter. Snapper and pearl perch are closed to take in all Queensland tidal waters from 15 July to 15 August.
Do South East Queensland charters go game fishing?

Some do, mainly in summer. Gold Coast operators target marlin, mahi mahi, wahoo and tuna from about November to February, and Brisbane charters often switch to trolling when the East Australian Current makes bottom fishing difficult.

sections.h: Destinations on the Fraser Coast and around Bundaberg

Full-day reef trips from Carlo Point and Tin Can Bay to Double Island Point and southern K'gari
Hervey Bay and K'gari
Small private sportfishing boats from Urangan for the flats, artificial reefs, Platypus Bay and Breaksea Spit
Bundaberg
Reef trips from Burnett Heads to inshore and wide reefs, plus calm-water Burnett River charters
Double Island Point
Reefs fished for snapper, pearl perch, parrotfish, coral trout and red emperor
Hervey Bay flats
Sight fishing on the tide for golden trevally, longtail tuna and juvenile black marlin
Platypus Bay
Mid-winter snapper ground over weed, reef, holes and wrecks
Hervey Bay artificial reefs and Moon Ledge
Inshore reef and ledge fishing within the bay
Breaksea Spit
About two hours each way from Urangan, for topwater giant trevally and Spanish mackerel
Bundaberg inshore and wide reefs
Sweetlip, snapper and Spanish mackerel inshore; coral trout and red emperor out toward the shelf
Burnett River
Bream, whiting, flathead, mangrove jack, grunter and blue salmon in calm water
Snapper
Late autumn to mid-winter in Hervey Bay; closed 15 July-15 August
Longtail tuna
About February to May in Hervey Bay
Golden trevally, queenfish and Spanish mackerel
Late winter and spring
Coral trout and red emperor
Year-round on Bundaberg's wider reefs, outside the October and November coral reef fin fish closures
Humpback whales
Often seen from Rainbow Beach boats between about May and October

p: Rainbow Beach trips leave between about 5 and 5:30am and operators confirm conditions the day before, so book flexible accommodation. Hervey Bay's channels are shallow and can be dangerous on a strong outgoing tide, while Bundaberg's port has no designated bar and no tidal restrictions.

Hervey Bay and the Great Sandy Strait sit in the Great Sandy Marine Park, so check the zoning map if you fish on your own. Bundaberg is roughly the southern limit of the coral reef fin fish spawning closures (latitude 24 50' S).

faq: Is Hervey Bay or Bundaberg better for reef fishing?

They suit different trips. Bundaberg charters run to coral reefs out toward the shelf for coral trout and red emperor, with no bar to cross. Hervey Bay charters are mostly small sportfishing boats chasing golden trevally, longtail tuna, queenfish and winter snapper in sheltered water.
Can you go fishing off K'gari (Fraser Island) on a charter?

Yes. Rainbow Beach boats fish reefs off southern K'gari, Hervey Bay guides fish the island's western side, Rooneys Point and Breaksea Spit, and some Hervey Bay charters collect guests from Kingfisher Bay Resort by arrangement.
Are there half-day fishing trips on the Fraser Coast?
In Hervey Bay and Bundaberg, yes. Rainbow Beach and Tin Can Bay charters run full days only, leaving about 5-5:30am and returning mid-afternoon.

sections.h: Destinations on the Southern Great Barrier Reef
items: Agnes Water and 1770
Day trips through Round Hill Creek to deep-water reefs, Bustard Head and, on longer days, the Bunker Group
Gladstone
Three- to ten-plus-day liveaboards to the Capricorn Bunker Group, Swain Reefs and Coral Sea
Yeppoon and the Capricorn Coast
Keppel Bay day trips, 18-36-hour extended runs and week-long Swains liveaboards from Rosslyn Bay
Capricorn and Bunker Group
Lady Musgrave, Fitzroy, Boult and Hoskyn reefs, roughly 45-75 km from the coastal ports
Swain Reefs
About 120 nautical miles off Gladstone, reached overnight on week-long liveaboards
Coral Sea reefs
Marion, Frederick, Kenn and Wreck reefs, 200-260 nm out, on ten-day trips for dogtooth tuna and wahoo
Keppel Bay reefs and wrecks
Red emperor, goldband snapper, large-mouth nannygai and coral trout off Yeppoon
Bustard Head and the 1770 wrecks
Mackerel, tuna, trevally and cobia year-round
Round Hill, Eurimbula and Pancake creeks
Mangrove jack, barramundi, queenfish, grunter and whiting

p: Day charters from 1770 and Yeppoon supply rods, bait and tackle and suit beginners. Liveaboards from Gladstone and Rosslyn Bay are mostly self-guided: you bring your own gear, fish from dories or tenders, and the catch is processed and frozen to take home. You often need a recreational boat licence to drive a dory, and many boats need a full group or let individuals join set trips.

Almost all the offshore grounds are inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group has many green (no-take) zones, including most of Heron Island and part of Wistari Reef. Charter skippers fish the open zones; on your own boat, check the current GBRMPA zoning map.

Agnes Water is about 5.5 hours' drive from Brisbane, Gladstone about six hours or an hour's flight, and Yeppoon about 45 km from Rockhampton. If the Round Hill Creek bar or the weather rules out a 1770 trip, Bundaberg and Gladstone boats also fish the southern reefs.

faq: Where is the closest Great Barrier Reef fishing to Brisbane?

The Town of 1770 and Agnes Water, about 5.5 hours' drive north of Brisbane, sit where the Great Barrier Reef begins. Day charters there fish reefs within about 15 nautical miles, and the Capricorn and Bunker Group lies roughly 45-75 km offshore.
How do you fish the Swain Reefs?

On a liveaboard. Boats leave Gladstone or Rosslyn Bay near Yeppoon, steam overnight about 120 nautical miles to the Swains, and fish for about a week, usually from dories. Some Yeppoon day boats reach the Swains on 18-36-hour extended trips in settled weather.
Can I fish around Heron Island?

Mostly no. Heron Island is largely green zone and part of neighbouring Wistari Reef is green zone, so fishing isn't allowed there. Open zones exist elsewhere in the Capricorn and Bunker Group, and charter skippers know where you can fish.

sections.h: Where to fish in South East Tasmania
items: Hobart & Storm Bay
Shared inshore trips from Margate Marina, private offshore charters, and Derwent estuary fly fishing
Tasman Peninsula
Eaglehawk Neck, Pirates Bay and Port Arthur for tuna, striped trumpeter, flathead and morwong
Frederick Henry Bay
Sheltered bay charters from Dodges Ferry for sand flathead, calamari, salmon and whiting

p: Pick a shared trip from Hobart for a short, calm-water outing with family or beginners, a Tasman Peninsula charter for tuna and deep reef fish, or a private charter if your group wants to choose the grounds. Some charters can arrange pick-ups from Hobart.

Rod-and-line sea fishing needs no licence, but diving for rock lobster or abalone does. Frederick Henry, Norfolk and Blackman bays are shark refuge areas where sharks, skates and rays other than elephantfish cannot be taken. Check the current NRE Tas rules for bag and size limits.

faq: Where is tuna fishing based in South East Tasmania?

Mainly at Eaglehawk Neck (Pirates Bay) and Port Arthur on the Tasman Peninsula, where local charters run tuna trips from about March to August. Hobart charters reach Storm Bay tuna grounds by private charter.
Which South East Tasmania fishing trip suits families?

Calm-water options are the shared trips from Margate Marina, which Diver's says mostly fish sheltered water and where children under 6 ride free, and Mr Flathead's Dodges Ferry bay charter on Frederick Henry Bay for flathead, calamari, salmon and whiting.

items: Central Highlands
Great Lake, Arthurs Lake, Penstock and Little Pine lagoons, and the Western Lakes from Miena
Launceston & the North
Brumbys Creek, South Esk, Macquarie, Meander, St Patricks and Mersey rivers, plus the Tamar estuary
Private fisheries
Currawong Lakes on the Eastern Tiers: no licence needed, access fees apply

p: Highland lakes offer polaroiding, tailing fish and big mayfly and beetle days but can be cold and windy; the lowland rivers are closer to Launceston accommodation, more sheltered, and suit half days. Many guides fish both and choose on the day.

Everyone 14 or older needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, including guided clients; short-term licences are available and some guides sell them. Launceston has direct flights from Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane, and highland guides such as Miena Guiding recommend arriving the night before.

faq: Should I base myself in Launceston or Miena for a trout trip?

Launceston suits river fishing and shorter days, with most venues within an hour; Miena puts you on Great Lake and the highland lagoons, and Miena Guiding starts its days with a 9am pick-up from local accommodation. Several guides run both.
Do guided trout clients need their own licence in Tasmania?

Yes. The Inland Fisheries Service says anyone 14 or older fishing inland waters needs a current angling licence, with no exemption for guided clients. Registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes are the exception.

p: Port Phillip is the easier, more sheltered option, with departures close to the city and Geelong and plenty of family-friendly trips. Western Port's strong tides and deep channels produce big spring snapper and gummy shark, and it gives the quickest run into Bass Strait from Hastings.
items: Melbourne & Port Phillip
Carrum, St Kilda, Mornington, Safety Beach, Blairgowrie, Queenscliff and Geelong departures
Western Port & Phillip Island
Hastings Boat Ramp, Western Port Marina and Stony Point departures
Shared snapper sessions
Five-hour trips, up to three a day in season, with seats sold individually
Family and bay trips
Two- to four-hour trips on calmer water; Geelong runs kids' clubs and under-10s fish free
Big-group charters
A 15 m vessel at Hastings takes private groups of up to 20; Pro Red uses affiliated boats for up to 20
Offshore Bass Strait
Kingfish, bluefin tuna and sharks from Hastings and Queenscliff, usually with a minimum age of 12

p: Bring your own Victorian Recreational Fishing Licence unless you are exempt; most operators don't sell them. Everyone must wear a life jacket crossing Port Phillip Heads. Trailered boats often confirm the ramp a few days before the trip, so check your booking message.

faq: Should I book a Port Phillip or a Western Port charter?

Pick Port Phillip for sheltered, family-friendly trips close to the city or Geelong, and Western Port for tidal snapper and gummy shark fishing from Hastings and the quickest run offshore. Several operators fish both and move ramps to follow the snapper.
How much does a Melbourne snapper charter cost?

Shared five-hour snapper sessions on the bays are typically about $220 per person, and whole-boat private charters start from around $1,300 to $1,760 depending on the boat. Check each operator's page for current prices.
Can I go offshore from Melbourne?

Yes. Hastings in Western Port and Queenscliff at Port Phillip Heads are the main launch points for Bass Strait trips targeting kingfish, southern bluefin tuna and sharks, from about mid-January to early April for kingfish and tuna.

items: Lake Mulwala and the Murray River
Lure fishing for Murray cod and golden perch from Yarrawonga
Lake Eildon
Trophy Murray cod and golden perch, with no cod closed season
Mansfield's rivers
Walk-and-wade trout on the Delatite, Howqua, Jamieson and King rivers
Goulburn River below Eildon
Drift-boat and bank fly fishing for trout around Thornton and Alexandra

p: Lake Mulwala and the Murray River are NSW waters, so a NSW recreational fishing licence applies there; some guides include it in the price. Lake Hume is the exception, where a Victorian licence is valid. Lake Eildon and the High Country rivers need a Victorian Recreational Fishing Licence unless you are exempt.

Many High Country rivers have no mobile reception, so guides give pick-up and return times and carry satellite messengers. Murray cod slot and bag limits differ between waters, so check the current VFA or NSW DPI rules before keeping a fish.

faq: Can I fish for Murray cod in spring?
Not in most waters: the closed season runs 1 September to 30 November, and guides switch to golden perch. Lake Eildon has no cod closed season, so guided cod fishing there can run all year.
Do I need fly-fishing experience for a guided trout trip?
No. High Country and Goulburn guides take first-timers through to experienced anglers, with tuition, waders and fly gear supplied, and some run beginner workshops.
Which licence do I need on Lake Mulwala?
A NSW recreational fishing licence, because the lake is classified as NSW water, whether you fish from a boat, kayak or the shore. Lake Mulwala Sportfishing includes the licence in its charter price.

items: Geraldton & the Abrolhos
Six-night Abrolhos live-aboards, Abrolhos day trips, rock lobster tours and near-coast day fishing from Batavia Coast Marina
Exmouth & Ningaloo
Billfish gameboats from Tantabiddi and Exmouth Marina, shared bottom-fishing days, and Ningaloo, island and Montebello live-aboards
Abrolhos Islands
Dhufish, pink snapper and baldchin groper (tagged charters only), coral trout, Spanish mackerel, tuna and rock lobster
Ningaloo and the shelf
Blue, black and striped marlin, sailfish, wahoo, mahi mahi and yellowfin tuna
Ningaloo Reef and islands
Red emperor, coral trout, spangled emperor, rankin cod, giant trevally and Spanish mackerel

sections.h: Rules that differ along the coast
p: Geraldton and the Abrolhos sit in the West Coast bioregion, where boat-based recreational demersal fishing is closed until spring 2027. There, only charters holding demersal tags can keep species such as dhufish. Exmouth is in the Gascoyne, where demersal fishing is open but new bag and size limits apply from 1 June 2026. Paying guests on licensed charters don't need a boat fishing licence anywhere on the coast. Check the current DPIRD rules before you go.

faq: Is Exmouth part of the Coral Coast?

Yes. Australia's Coral Coast tourism region runs about 1,100km from Cervantes, north of Perth, to Ningaloo Reef, so it includes Geraldton, the Abrolhos Islands, Kalbarri, Shark Bay, Coral Bay and Exmouth.
Where on the Coral Coast can I still keep dhufish?

At the Abrolhos, only on a charter that holds West Coast demersal tags, because boat-based recreational demersal fishing in the West Coast bioregion is closed until spring 2027. Further north in the Gascoyne, around Exmouth, demersal fishing is open under the current DPIRD limits.
Which is better for marlin, Geraldton or Exmouth?

Exmouth. Its charters are built around billfish, because the continental shelf lies close to the North West Cape, with blue marlin trips from October to April and Gulf sailfish in spring. Geraldton charters focus on Abrolhos reef fish, pelagics and rock lobster, though some live-aboards troll for marlin on wider days.

Creek and Roebuck Bay trips, offshore reef days with accommodation pickup, sailfish and black marlin gameboats, private lure and fly sportfishing
Kimberley
Nine-day live-aboards from Broome, the Kuri Bay fly-in lodge in Camden Sound, and Aboriginal-guided tours on Balanggarra Country near Kununurra and Wyndham

Broome creek trip for barramundi and threadfin, or a private sportfishing charter
One day, family or group
Broome offshore reef day on a large boat with lunch and pickup
Billfish
Broome gameboats from April to November, including sailfish on fly
A week or more
Kimberley live-aboard (up to six anglers) or a four- to seven-night Kuri Bay lodge stay
Cultural fishing
Catch-and-cook days, overnight safaris and tagalongs with a Balanggarra guide

p: Saltwater crocodiles live in almost every waterway that holds barramundi, so stand back from the edge and never clean fish at the water. Tides can exceed eight to nine metres, which is why creek trips are timed to the tide. Demersal fishing is open in the North West, but new North Coast bag and size limits applied from 1 June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules. Paying guests on licensed charters don't need a boat fishing licence.

faq: What is the difference between Broome and Kimberley fishing charters?

Broome charters are mostly day trips from town: creek barramundi, offshore reef fishing and sailfish. Kimberley trips go much further and take longer, using live-aboards that leave Broome for nine days, fly-in lodges reached by seaplane, or guided trips out of Kununurra and the East Kimberley.
When is the best time to fish the Kimberley and Broome?

The dry season from about April to October has the calmest weather. Kimberley coast live-aboards fish from April to August, Rowley Shoals and Scott Reef trips run from late August to November, and Broome billfish days run April to November. Creek barramundi fishing continues in the wetter months, and the Ord River fishes year round.
Can you keep reef fish in the North West?

Yes. The West Coast demersal closure doesn't apply in the North West, and tourism bodies note that recreational and charter demersal fishing remains available there. Bag and size limits changed from 1 June 2026, so check the current DPIRD rules. Some live-aboards, though, are catch and release apart from fish eaten aboard.

items: Cairns
The largest fleet: shared and private reef boats, Trinity Inlet estuary trips, river days to the Mulgrave and Russell, Lake Tinaroo barra and marlin game boats
Port Douglas
About an hour to the reef on the big boats; small sportfishing boats mix fringing reefs, the Low Isles and estuaries; liveaboards to the Ribbon Reefs
Daintree
Barramundi, mangrove jack and mud crabs on more than 25 km of navigable river, with Snapper Island and river-mouth reefs on calm days

p: Shared reef days cost about $340–$350 per person from Cairns or Port Douglas, and shared estuary half days start at about $120–$200. Private river and estuary trips are usually $650–$1,320 per boat for four to six hours, private reef or GT days about $1,650–$1,900, and marlin game boats about $3,200–$3,600 per day.

Shared reef boats with handlines and rods, or a half day in Trinity Inlet or the Port Douglas estuaries
Barramundi anglers
Private river guides on the Daintree, Cairns rivers or Lake Tinaroo, often with hotel pick-up
Sportfishing and fly
Topwater GT on the reef, flats and island fly trips, and light-tackle juvenile marlin
Game fishing
Giant black marlin liveaboards of three to seven days from September to mid-December

p: Cairns Airport is the arrival point for the region. Port Douglas is about 60 km north of Cairns, under an hour's drive, and the Daintree River ferry crossing is further north again on the road to Cape Tribulation. Several guides fish Cairns, Port Douglas and the Daintree, so one booking can cover more than one area.

Great Barrier Reef trips carry the Environmental Management Charge (reef tax), $8.50 per person from 1 April 2026, and many reef boats now add a fuel levy. Coral reef fin fish and Spanish mackerel have seasonal closures in October and November, and east-coast barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January. Saltwater crocodiles live in every river and estuary here, so keep well back from the water's edge.

faq: Should I fish from Cairns or Port Douglas?

Both reach the Great Barrier Reef. Cairns has the larger fleet and the most shared reef boats; Port Douglas boats reach the outer reef sooner, about an hour on the larger boats, and small boats there can retreat to the estuaries in wind. Many guides pick up from either town.
Where can I catch a barramundi in Tropical North Queensland?

Guides fish Trinity Inlet in Cairns, the Mulgrave and Russell rivers, the Port Douglas estuaries and the Daintree River, outside the 1 November to 31 January closure. Lake Tinaroo on the Atherton Tablelands holds stocked metre-plus barramundi and is fished during the saltwater closure.
When is black marlin season in Far North Queensland?

Giant black marlin gather on the reef edge between Cairns and Lizard Island from early September to mid-December, usually fished on liveaboards. Juvenile black marlin are caught on light tackle closer to Cairns and Port Douglas through much of the year.

sections.h: Destinations in the Whitsundays and Mackay
items: Whitsundays
Coral Sea Marina (Airlie Beach), Hamilton Island Marina and Cape Gloucester Resort; shared half and full days, private outer reef trips and game boats
Mackay
Offshore reef days from Hay Point, fly and lure guiding on the Seaforth flats, and impoundment barramundi on Kinchant and Teemburra dams

p: Shared Whitsunday reef trips cost about $250–$335 per person for a half day and $450–$480 for a full day; private boats run about $1,800–$5,150 depending on length and vessel. A full offshore day from Hay Point is about $500 per person with a minimum of four.
items: Families
Shared half days around the islands, many of which clean and fillet your catch
Reef fish to eat
Full-day or extended outer reef trips for red emperor and coral trout
Sportfish
Sailfish and black marlin from Hamilton Island; GT, permit and golden trevally on Mackay's flats
Barramundi
Mackay creeks in the warmer months, and stocked dams year-round

p: The whole region is inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, so zoning applies; one Airlie Beach operator holds Yellow Zone certification for areas many charters cannot fish. Spanish mackerel north of 22°S are limited to one per person on the east coast and have closed seasons in October and November. One Mackay offshore operator brings all fish back whole, citing the rules on filleting at sea.

faq: Is fishing better in the Whitsundays or Mackay?

They suit different trips. The Whitsundays have the most shared and private reef charters and easy island scenery, while Mackay adds fly and lure flats fishing, net-free creeks for barramundi and stocked dams. Mackay offshore days leave Hay Point, about 30 minutes south of town.
Can I fish the outer reef from the Whitsundays?

Yes, on longer trips. The outer reef is about 40 nautical miles from Airlie Beach, so it is fished on 8-hour private or 10–11 hour extended trips; half days and most shared trips fish the island grounds.
Can I catch barramundi near Mackay in summer?
Saltwater barramundi are closed from 1 November to 31 January, but Kinchant and Teemburra dams are stocked and stay open, and local guides run half and full days there for one or two anglers.

items: Townsville and Magnetic Island
Full-boat and mixed-group reef trips of 9–23 hours from Breakwater Marina; private inshore and offshore charters from Horseshoe Bay
Hinchinbrook and Lucinda
Guided barramundi in the channel and Missionary Bay, offshore days to the islands and reef, and multi-day accommodated packages

p: Townsville's big reef boats are mostly booked as a whole boat (about $4,500 for a 9-hour shoal trip, $6,800 for a 13-hour reef day), with single seats on mixed-group trips when the weather suits. Hinchinbrook guides take two to four anglers, about $720–$1,050 a day depending on group size.

Long Townsville day or overnight trips for red emperor and nannygai
A trophy barramundi
Private Hinchinbrook Channel days, timed to the tides
Families on holiday
Private half days around Magnetic Island's bays

p: Launch at Dungeness from half tide up; near low tide the ramp end can be exposed and the channel bar impassable. Long Townsville reef trips usually supply bait, tackle and ice but not meals. The channel and creeks are crocodile habitat and lie inside the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park, so check zoning and keep back from the bank.

faq: How far is Hinchinbrook from Townsville?

Lucinda, the main launch point for the Hinchinbrook Channel, is about 1.5 hours' drive north of Townsville and about 2.5 hours south of Cairns. Some Hinchinbrook packages include Townsville Airport transfers.
Can I join a reef fishing trip from Townsville on my own?
Yes. Mixed-group charters sell individual places on 12–13 hour reef trips for up to 12 people. They are opened when the weather suits, often at short notice, and need enough bookings to go ahead.

sections.h: Destinations in Cape York and the Gulf
items: Weipa and Cape York
Accommodated packages of four days or more, a fishing lodge with private chef, and mothership trips to remote rivers, the Torres Strait and east-coast reef flats
Karumba and the Gulf
Half- and full-day Norman River and offshore charters, dedicated barramundi days, multi-day and remote camping trips

p: Weipa has twice-daily QantasLink flights from Cairns on most days, with a one-bag, 23 kg luggage limit, and guides collect from the airport. Karumba visitors usually fly into Normanton and transfer by road, or drive across from the east coast. Cape York motherships are joined at Horn Island, flying from Cairns.

Gulf rules differ from the east coast. The Gulf barramundi closure starts on 7 October, and the Gulf Spanish mackerel limit is 3 per person or 6 per boat, higher on licensed charter trips of 48 hours or more. Fishing here is largely catch and release, mobile coverage is limited, and crocodiles, box jellyfish and stingrays mean you wade only where your guide says it is safe.

faq: Is Weipa or Karumba better for barramundi?

Both are well known for barramundi. Weipa offers more variety, with permit, golden trevally and tuna on the flats and offshore, and most trips are multi-day packages. Karumba focuses on the Norman River and Gulf, with dedicated barra charters from February to April and September to early October.
How long should a Cape York fishing trip be?

Most Weipa packages run four to seven days including travel days, and Cape York mothership trips are five to six fishing days. Karumba has half- and full-day charters as well as multi-day and remote camping trips.
When is the barramundi closed season in the Gulf of Carpentaria?

The Gulf closed season starts on 7 October, earlier than the east coast's 1 November start. Check the current Queensland closed-season page for the end date before you book, and plan barra-focused Gulf trips for autumn or September.
